1326	## 4. Evaluation and proof verification
1327	
1328	The deterministic evaluator consumes only the Plan-bound, schema-admitted
1329	finite fact views, Coverage, imported evidence, declarative program, policy and
1330	waivers. The declarative rule program defines the exact subject enumeration,
1331	relation/rung, typed field filter, quantifier, deterministic work bound and
1332	emission condition for each predicate. Query planning is an optimization only:
1333	a retained full-scan reference must agree on selected facts. Neither a provider
1334	nor a witness supplies its own expected result or filter. All consumed data are
1335	listed in the proof's evaluationInputRefs; no hidden lookup is allowed.
1336	
1337	A predicate proof binds rule, subject, predicate, operation, admitted inputs,
1338	scopes, value and a retained witness digest. The closed witness record contains

1338	scopes, value and a retained witness digest. The closed witness record contains
1339	schemaVersion=2, program predicate digest, sorted matching fact IDs, sorted
1340	Coverage IDs, optional integer count limit and sorted child-predicate IDs.
1341	The program predicate digest is the §3 `program-predicate` record, which addresses
1342	the exact node of the admitted rule program this proof discharges; the predicate
1343	ID and the child predicate IDs are that section's node addresses, not free
1344	labels. An atomic witness names no children; boolean witnesses name only earlier
1345	nodes in the same subject/rule DAG, and each named child must itself be proven
1346	for the same rule and subject. Predicate IDs are unique and the DAG is bounded
1347	by the rule program's admitted work bound. Witness facts must be exactly those
1348	selected by the program over the complete admitted view, not merely a subset
1349	chosen by the producer. Counts count distinct selected fact IDs. The verifier
1350	recomputes scope membership, matches, completeness and each result, and then
1351	recomputes finding fingerprints, findings, rule outcomes and aggregate verdict.
1352	Missing witness bytes is retention loss, not a false predicate.
1353	
1354	| Predicate | Positive/complete case | Incomplete case |
1355	|---|---|---|
1356	| exists | true on a matching fact; false only on complete absence | true on a known match, otherwise indeterminate |
1357	| none | false on a known match; true only on complete absence | false on a known match, otherwise indeterminate |
1358	| count-at-most N | false once more than N distinct matches exist; true when complete count ≤ N | false above N, otherwise indeterminate |
1359	| all-covered | true only with admitted resolution-complete coverage for the requested universe/rung | indeterminate |
1360	| and / or / not | strong Kleene three-valued logic; false dominates and, true dominates or | unresolved value propagates unless dominated |
1361	
1362	Completeness means the native contract's examined partition **and** resolution
1363	and closed-world requirements. An unresolved `m[k]()` can never establish
1364	no-consumer merely because the enumerator visited all subjects. Runtime unhit
1365	observations never supply universal static completeness. A rule expression that
1366	is true produces its declared outcome; findings arise only from the program's
1367	emission condition. A false condition is a retained no-match proof. An
1368	indeterminate required predicate is retained with typed deficiency. A schema,
1369	identity or interpreter fault is an operational failure, not a fourth logical
1370	truth value and not an authoritative Run. Aggregate policy fail dominates
1371	indeterminate, which dominates pass; a required operational fault has D9's
1372	operational precedence even if other steps have committed failing Runs.
1373	
1374	Before sealing, the host independently replays the admitted deterministic
1375	program against the retained closure and compares the complete normalized
1376	result (all predicate outcomes, omissions, findings and verdict), not just a
1377	checksum supplied by the producer. This verifier is first-party trusted code;
1378	this is reproducible verification, not a proof of mathematical soundness or a
1379	sandbox against a malicious host. Semantic conformance uses independent
1380	oracles and mutation cases. The exact evaluator executable, declarative program,
1381	input closure and witness bytes are retained, so an independent installation
1382	can replay without trusting the original result flags. No old Python route
1383	region is executed to decide product authority.
1384	
1385	Verification reads retained objects and creates an operational verification
1386	receipt. Regeneration executes the exact retained producer and Plan input
1387	closure into a candidate namespace, verifies each expected semantic identity,
1388	and publishes recovered availability only if all required bytes agree. A
1389	mismatch is an operational regeneration verification refusal: `HOST.IO_FAILURE`
1390	(class `operational-failed`, faultCause `host-io`, exit4), domain detail
1391	`evidence.regeneration-mismatch`. It cannot replace the sealed Run. New
1392	source or policy creates a new Plan/Run. Expired or
1393	revoked permission cannot be resurrected by a matching hash. A miss recomputes
1394	normally; a corrupt hit is quarantined and disclosed before any permitted retry.
1395	
1396	**Constructing a cache key and admitting a hit are two different acts, and only
1397	the second is an admission.** Key construction is pure and deterministic: exact
1398	schema admission and canonical order over the `cache-key` record, nothing more. It
1399	reads no bytes and resolves no reference, so a host may compute it before loading
1400	anything and miss cheaply; it is a lookup key and grants nothing. **Finding bytes
1401	under a matching key is not authority.** An entry may be consumed only against
1402	exactly the closure the Run itself requires: the stage spec retained and joined to
1403	this Plan, the producing closure retained and Plan-selected, every `scopeIds`
1404	member a retained `subject-scope` of this snapshot, the output schema document
1405	retained, and every `inputRefs` entry resolved through the same
1406	`x-opensip-digest-domains` registry the Run uses — so a consumed native context
1407	must be one this Plan selected, a consumed import must be one this Plan selected,
1408	and nothing is admitted under a guessed payload-domain schema. A bare
1409	`coverage-payload`, `import-payload` or `fact-payload` reference is refused as an
1410	authoritative root rather than resolved by guesswork; those are reached only
1411	through their owning object. A hit that clears all of this is reusable producer
1412	output, never evidence authority, and it never replaces or re-seals a Run. The
1413	same record and the same admission apply to a regeneration key; only the H domain
1414	differs, and a regeneration whose result disagrees remains the
1415	`evidence.regeneration-mismatch` refusal above.

1417	## 5. Durable custody and failure protocol
1418	
1419	Default `opensip`/`analyze` is DURABLE_AUTHORITATIVE under CD-RT-5. The host
1420	reports retention origin DEFAULTED and durable-unbounded posture before first
1421	write; the command's documented effect is admission of the project marker and
1422	private registry/store, followed by an authoritative Run. No implicit policy
1423	file is written. Explicit retention overrides have independent byte/time/count
1424	bounds with provenance; failure to satisfy an authoritative request never
1425	silently demotes it to ephemeral. `--ephemeral` is explicitly non-authoritative,
1426	uses temporary custody, mints no authoritative commit receipt and cannot satisfy
1427	baseline adoption, repair or authoritative replay prerequisites.
1428	
1429	The storage-root admission still applies the inherited sync, backup and private
1430	custody classifications separately. A detected backup-managed root requires an
1431	explicit storage-policy choice before the first source-derived write (TM V17):
1432	select another admitted root, choose explicit ephemeral mode, or acknowledge
1433	backup custody for this invocation with `--allow-backup-custody` (or the
1434	corresponding already-admitted host storage-policy record). CI never prompts;
1435	without that explicit choice it refuses REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED with detail
1436	`storage.backup-choice-required`, before creating evidence. The acknowledgement
1437	is retained as operational custody metadata; it does not alter semantic Run
1438	identity or silently write a policy file. UNKNOWN backup status is disclosed as
1439	unknown, never as not-backed-up. Purge never claims deletion of external copies.
1440	Sync/upload roots and group/ACL exposure retain their separate admission rules;
1441	a backup acknowledgement is not a network-export or shared-storage grant.
1442	
1443	Exactly one per-project writer holds the lifecycle lease/fence through source
1444	admission, evaluation and atomic commit. Read-only clients use a consistent
1445	committed ledger snapshot and never wait while holding a lock needed by the
1446	writer. Global trust admission and revocation use the security contract's lock
1447	order. SQLite WAL, transaction settings, fsync/atomic-rename carrier and crash
1448	reconciliation retain the reviewed lifecycle carrier's native obligations;
1449	the reference model here tests the semantic transition, not OS durability.
1450	
1451	Commit order:
1452	
1453	1. Validate closure and independently replay proof; compute all final IDs.
1454	2. Write immutable blobs and descriptors to private temporary files, verify
1455	   digest/length, fsync files, atomically publish under digest, fsync directories.
1456	3. In one synchronous ledger transaction insert Run manifest, object references,
1457	   retained availability generation, baseline/other authorized pins and a commit
1458	   receipt with ExecutionId, namespace, monotonic sequence, inventory digest,
1459	   signer and immutable assurance; commit and satisfy the carrier's barriers.
1460	4. Only then acknowledge commitment. Required rendering/delivery is later and
1461	   cannot rewrite the Run. Receipt signing is operational custody evidence and
1462	   excluded from semantic IDs; the receipt authenticates RunId and inventory.
1463	
1464	A failure before step 3 publishes no authoritative Run. Orphan blobs are
1465	unreferenced and eligible for GC after reconciliation. A crash after ledger
1466	commit but before acknowledgement is `durability-undetermined` to the caller,
1467	exit 4, with an ExecutionId for read-only recovery. Recovery checks the ledger
1468	and actual objects; it returns committed or failed, never repeats a repository
1469	mutation. Duplicate retry can share a Run but has a separate attempt receipt.
1470	An acknowledged Run with missing/corrupt objects becomes partially available or
1471	corrupt; the host does not pretend it was never sealed.
1472	
1473	Sealed assurance is immutable: verified means exact identity+proof checks at
1474	seal; verifiable also commits the verification closure; replayable also commits
1475	all exact admitted producer executables and source/input closure. The default
1476	authoritative profile requires replayable retention at seal. Current
1477	availability is a separate monotonic-generation record: retained, partial,
1478	expired, purged, corrupt or unavailable, with exact missing references and
1479	cause. Availability may improve through verified restoration or regeneration;
1480	sealed assurance and historical verdict never change. A query reports both.
1481	
1482	Retention roots include every live Run's required closure, active baseline,
1483	authorized repair prerequisite and backup/export operation pin. Automatic
1484	expiry respects these pins and all independent policy bounds; it refuses a
1485	new durable admission if the required closure cannot be retained within bounds.
1486	A direct purge of a pinned Run refuses unless the explicit destructive purge
1487	also revokes the named pins after disclosing consequences. That refusal has a
1488	registered public projection and this contract does not restate it: the
1489	foundation-owned detail `evidence.pinned` projects as `request-rejected`,
1490	`REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED`, exit 2, carrying the closed
1491	`common.schema.json#/$defs/PinnedPurgeDisclosure` — the RunId, the complete
1492	current `activePins` inventory sorted uniquely by `pinId`, and the three ordered
1493	consequences `named-pins-revoked`,
1494	`dependent-evidence-replay-unavailable`, `sealed-history-retained` — exactly as
1495	**workflows-and-surfaces §12** specifies. No pin is omitted, truncated or
1496	aggregated into a count. Neither that disclosure nor any flag confers authority:
1497	a later destructive attempt still requires the explicit lifecycle authorization
1498	and disclosure of its then-current complete pin set, and a changed pin inventory
1499	requires renewed disclosure before destruction. Purge retains the
1500	minimal sealed manifest, provenance and tombstone but deletes unshared evidence
1501	bytes by reachability GC; shared bytes survive until the final reference is
1502	removed. Purged is not deleted-history. The user may separately destroy the
1503	whole project store/marker under lifecycle authorization; no indefinite privacy
1504	claim is made for backups or exports already outside that store.
1505	
1506	A retention decision never changes a fact, Coverage, finding or Run identity.
1507	It never turns expired evidence into `no match`. Query of retained manifest is
1508	allowed after purge and states evidence unavailable. Query requiring actual
1509	proof, comparison baseline or repair input refuses with
1510	REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED and `evidence.{expired,purged,missing,corrupt}`
1511	before evaluation (exit 2); inability during a selected operation is HOST.IO_FAILURE
1512	with evidence detail (exit 4). Successfully admitted partial native inputs may
1513	instead produce an indeterminate Run (exit 3) under the native and D9 contracts.
1514	These are different event positions, not interchangeable error spellings.
1515	
1516	Backup/export holds a read snapshot plus short-lived object pins, writes a
1517	bounded relative-path inventory, hashes and verifies every object, then seals
1518	the bundle. Import checks path traversal, symlinks, sizes, duplicate paths,
1519	cryptographic identities and all referenced schemas before publishing anything.
1520	Source provenance/authenticity is reported separately from hash integrity.
1521	Trust floors, current authorization and local custody receipts are never
1522	restored backwards from an evidence backup. Portable baseline details are in
1523	the workflow contract. An import cannot silently claim a remote Run was locally
1524	evaluated: its imported-custody receipt names origin and local verification.

1526	## 6. Required implementation conformance
1527	
1528	Reference checks cover exact numeric and canonical encodings, wrong-source and
1529	wrong-Plan joins, identity changes for each semantic input, operational identity
1530	exclusion, universal negatives under incomplete resolution, proof tampering,
1531	retention/purge invariance and crash acknowledgement states. They additionally
1532	assert the digest law mechanically: that every 64-hex field carries a registered
1533	representation, that each new closed record reproduces an independently computed
1534	canonical digest vector and moves under every single-field mutation, and that a
1535	complete Run with a non-empty native context set closes while an altered frame, a
1536	missing preimage, a wrong preimage, an unregistered H domain, a raw payload
1537	offered as an H identity and a hidden input each refuse with a typed cause. They
1538	also assert that a fully re-framed and re-keyed Run built around a context the
1539	native boundary refuses — contradicting honored options, a compiler or runtime
1540	digest outside the tool closure, an incomplete stdlib inventory, a component
1541	digest that is not the retained tree's, a compiler version not from the manifest,
1542	a universe contradicting its context, or a config graph or lockfile path outside
1543	the snapshot — is refused with that boundary's own typed refusal string. They
1544	exercise a complete Rust universe/fact/Coverage Run alongside the TypeScript one,
1545	with the nested dependency, features, config-projection and prepared-output
1546	records retained and joined; and they separate cache key construction from cache
1547	hit admission, showing that a key needs no bytes while a hit needs the Run's whole
1548	closure. Their source pins
1549	and independent review are part of D-372. They do not qualify a native carrier.
1550	
1551	Before shipping, the exact implementation must additionally demonstrate:
1552	all supported platform fsync/SQLite/process-death cases; concurrent readers and
1553	writers plus trust revocation; independent replay across machines; missing,
1554	corrupt, stale and wrong-tenant closure rejection; hostile archive import; GC
1555	with shared references; backup restoration preserving trust floors; and public
1556	D9/CLI/JSON/SARIF/HTML/agent parity. Those are implementation acceptance criteria
1557	under existing G gates, not unresolved design alternatives.
1558	
1559	### Reference lifecycle joins
1560	
1561	The reference store instantiates closed commit-receipt and availability records.
1562	An availability transition increments generation and never rewrites a sealed Run
1563	or its original assurance. Read-only `recover(ExecutionId)` inspects the committed
1564	receipt after a lost acknowledgement and never repeats effects. Verified restoration
1565	requires the same complete identity closure and replay result before availability
1566	returns to retained; a regeneration mismatch refuses. Physical fsync, authenticated
1567	receipt signing, shared-blob deletion and OS crash recovery remain implementation
1568	qualification obligations; the reference transitions do not claim to execute them.
1569	
1570	The security chapter's three lease modes refine the inherited single-writer rule:
1571	immutable readers coexist with the append writer; exclusive migration/purge acquires
1572	the writer lease and reader exclusion. No second writer is permitted.
1573	
1574	At Run closure, every Plan-selected import re-admits its retained canonical SourceCorrespondence. An exact-snapshot import must name the Plan snapshot. VCS-revision imports require a retained, canonical admitted SourceMappingV1 to that snapshot, with inventory-matching source digests and the current clean revision; an unmapped/stale intake artifact may remain available for inspection but cannot be selected as an analyzed Plan input. Intake storage does not establish this source join. The authenticated importer/evaluator still owns payload-schema, observation-scope and polarity admission; rehashing an opaque import is insufficient. The reference closure reuses the same workflow import/mapping schema admission functions so the source law has one implementation.
1575	
1576	The semantic grant's `prepare-code` operation is present exactly when it projects trusted-repository-code preparation principals. Their provenance comes from consumed admitted host-prepared inputs; no test-runner operation or principal is added. Verification/replay checks these immutable bindings without reusing expired operational grants.
1577	
1578	The expected VCS build context is explicit, never inferred from the imported claim. The host may select one analysis-spec parameter whose schemaDigest is the raw SHA-256 of `foundation/import-source-context.schema.json` and whose payloadDigest binds canonical ImportSourceContextV1 `{schemaVersion:1, declaredBuildIds:[...]}`. These expected labels come from the separately admitted analysis request/build configuration; the importer cannot nominate its own expected labels. No parameter means an empty set; more than one is refused. Labels are declarations, not proof: source mapping remains mandatory. Run closure reconstructs workflow §4's binding from this retained parameter and the snapshot's VCS observation, then applies the same staleness function (both dirty flags, revision, expected build label and admitted mapping). A label not in the expected set is wrong-build and cannot become a Plan-selected import. The schema bytes and payload are retained with the Plan parameters for independent replay.
1579	
1580	Snapshot capture consumes the same admitted boundary inventory as native discovery. The host obtains it from successful security discovery, passes it unchanged to native discovery/membership and the shared scope descriptor, and removes nested-repository, nested-project and directory-custody-excluded paths before opening or hashing snapshot source bytes. The remaining paths are only capture candidates: per-file custody, safe handles and exact hashing still precede source admission. Boundary exclusion anchors enter the Plan's scope descriptor and their operational provenance is retained beside it. The host reference join admits one inventory; caller-supplied alternative boundary lists or substituted marker sets are refused. Discovery's dependency-tree pruning is an analysis-unit rule; explicitly required native dependency read-set bytes require separate custody/closure admission and cannot cross a nested authority boundary.
1581	
1582	Every Plan with selected import2 inputs also requires read-import in its semantic grant. This includes imported-inert preparation. Close_run enforces this operation/input join as well as prepare-code/principal equality; the later consuming-Plan admission separately validates the actual preparedResolution provenance.
1583	
1584	
1585	The reference closure entry point reports a missing promised object/blob as EvidenceUnavailable carrying the closed operational-failed/HOST.IO_FAILURE/host-io termination with evidence.missing and the missing reference. It never emits a bare lookup error or turns missing witness bytes into a false predicate or admission rejection. This models the host's retained-byte/custody observation boundary. Untrusted malformed records still receive exact schema/identity admission refusal; an inventory of available retained bytes does not authorize rewriting the assurance of a sealed Run.

113	
114	| Mode id | Recognition | Universe | Notes |
115	|---|---|---|---|

123	**This table selects a MODE; it does not discover units.** No Recognition cell
124	mints a unit. For the five rows that name a **compilation** universe —
125	`ts-tsconfig`, `js-allowjs`, `js-synthesized`, `rust-cargo` and
126	`rust-cargo-prepared` — the cell is read **after** §1.4 U-1 has yielded a unit of
127	that language family, because those modes describe a program and a program needs
128	one. **`syntax-only` carries no such prerequisite and must not be read as if it
129	did:** it is the compiler-free path, it has no compilation unit at all (§1.2's
130	third-universe paragraph and §6.3's grammar dialect branch both depend on that),
131	and it is exactly what serves a repository in which U-1 yields **no** TS or Rust
132	unit. A file reached that way is `syntax-only` membership with `unitOrdinal: null`
133	under U-4, not a member of an invented unit. U-1 is the specific model — the closed `WorkspaceUnitV2` record,
134	the exactly-once `FileMembershipRowV1` law and the marker precedence
135	`tsconfig.json` > `jsconfig.json` > `package.json` — and a `tsjs` unit exists only
136	where a directory holds one of those three markers. So a directory of bare `.js`
137	files with no marker is **not** a unit: under U-4 each such file is
138	`syntax-only` with reason `no-program-unit-for-language`, never a program member,
139	and no `js-synthesized` program is minted for them. An
140	earlier wording of the `js-synthesized` row read as an independent recognition
141	test ("`package.json` present **or** any `.js` file under the unit"), and an
142	implementer taking it alone would have minted units for bare-`.js` directories,
143	changing unit membership and therefore the Plan. The disjunct was never reachable
144	under U-1 — with no `tsconfig.json`, no `jsconfig.json` and no `package.json`
145	there is no unit for a `.js` file to be "under" — and the cell now says what it
146	always meant: within a U-1 unit whose marker is `package.json`, `.js` files are
147	program roots.
148	
149	**The syntax-only universe (CB3-MUST-3).** This column previously read
150	"none (syntax-all provider)", and that made the mode's own advertised cells
151	unrepresentable. `fact2` and `subject-scope` both **require** a
152	`native-semantic-universe` h-identity, that domain set held exactly the
153	TypeScript and Rust universes, and there is no null branch — so a
154	`declares@syntactic` or `clones@normalized-body-hash` fact in `syntax-only`
155	mode, and every `file`/`package`/`vcs-change` fact in a repository containing
156	no TypeScript and no Rust unit at all, could mint no fact and no scope. An
157	implementer had to invent a third domain, invent a null branch on a required
158	identity field, or quietly narrow this table.
159	
160	The registered answer is a third universe, `native.semantic-universe.syntax.v2`,
161	over a third native context, `native.context.syntax.v2`. Making the universe
162	fields nullable was rejected: it would delete the invariant that every fact
163	states what produced it, and would leave "which grammar read this body"
164	unanswerable for exactly the facts that depend on the answer.
165	
166	- **What it carries.** The context holds one thing: the installed
167	  `SyntaxGrammarBundleV1`, pinned the way a toolchain is — an admitted
168	  `kind=grammar` closure, a `parserVersion` that must equal that closure
169	  manifest's `semanticVersion`
170	  (`native.syntax-grammar-version-not-from-manifest`), and every grammar
171	  definition, the bundle manifest and the normalizer specification present in
172	  the retained tree. It has no toolchain, no stdlib, no lockfile, no
173	  `node_modules` layout and no config graph, because a grammar-only analysis
174	  reads none of them. A syntax-only context that named a compiler would assert
175	  semantics the mode never computes.
176	- **What the universe commits.** The admitted context plus the **selected**
177	  grammar set. Selecting a different set is a different universe, exactly as
178	  selecting different compilation targets is for Rust, so what was parsed is
179	  visible to every consumer instead of being an invisible default. A selection
180	  naming a grammar the bundle does not contain refuses
181	  (`native.syntax-grammar-not-in-bundle`). The constant
182	  `resolutionAttempted=false` is carried so no consumer can read the universe
183	  as a resolution claim.
184	- **The body dialect axis.** `body-language-version.dialect` gains a third
185	  branch, `{grammarVariant}`. A syntax-only analysis has no compilation unit, so
186	  it has no edition to select and no program to join; claiming `{edition: 2021}`
187	  for a `.rs` body read without Cargo would fabricate compiler semantics. One
188	  suffix must map to one grammar
189	  (`native.syntax-grammar-suffix-ambiguous`), longest match wins, and a suffix
190	  with no bundled grammar refuses rather than being folded into a neighbour —
191	  which is what keeps `unsupported-file / no-bundled-grammar` an honest
192	  classification. Because it is a distinct branch, **a grammar-parsed body never
193	  mints the same identity as a compiler-parsed one over the same bytes.** That
194	  is required: a grammar parse and a compiler parse are different
195	  interpretations, and equating them would be a false clone claim.
196	- **Capability is not widened.** A `syntax-only` universe carries only the
197	  inventory rungs, the `syntactic` rungs and `clones@normalized-body-hash`.
198	  `imports`/`references`/`calls`/`types`/`reachability` remain
199	  `language-tier-unsupported` under it, `unresolved-edge` stays unavailable
200	  because no resolution was attempted, and a universal-negative predicate still
201	  requires its own complete `CoverageResultV3`. Nothing here lets a syntax-only
202	  Run claim a resolved or type fact.
203	- **The bundled grammar set is closed, and it has SEVEN languages.** The host
204	  bundles grammars for `rust`, `typescript`, `javascript`, `json`, `toml`,
205	  `markdown` and `yaml`; the shared discovery rule routes all fourteen of their
206	  suffixes to membership `syntax-only`, reason `grammar-only`. An earlier
207	  revision of this section let the grammar descriptor name only the three code
208	  languages and asserted equality with the `body-language-version` `languageId`
209	  enum as a drift check. That check proved the enum matched itself: it could not
210	  express the four data/document grammars the host has always shipped, so the
211	  promise directly above — *any* file whose extension maps to a bundled grammar —
212	  was unrepresentable for them. The descriptor now covers exactly the bundled
213	  set, and each row declares its **`syntaxClass`**.
214	
215	**`code` versus `data-document`: the distinction the contracts already draw.**
216	This is not a new narrowing; it is an existing law made machine-readable.
217	
218	- **`code`** — `rust`, `typescript`, `javascript`. §6.3 defines body spans as
219	  function, method, closure/lambda, `impl` item and block bodies, publishes the
220	  L2/L3 normalisation tables for exactly these languages, and puts
221	  `languageId ∈ {typescript, javascript, rust}` in the clone preimage. These
222	  grammars bear clone body identity and the code-construct syntax relations, and
223	  their `languageId` **must** be a member of the `body-language-version` enum.
224	- **`data-document`** — `json`, `toml`, `markdown`, `yaml`. These formats have no
225	  such body spans, and this kit publishes **no** tokenisation, `literalKind`
226	  mapping or normalisation law for them anywhere. Their files are grammar-only
227	  members — accounted, inventoried, and never `unsupported-file` — bearing
228	  `file`/`package`/`vcs-change` inventory evidence under the syntax universe.
229	  They mint **no** body identity, no suffix of theirs appears in the grammar
230	  dialect table, and their `languageId` **must not** be in the
231	  `body-language-version` enum, since it could never appear in a clone preimage.
232	
233	Both directions are enforced at grammar-bundle admission: a data grammar
234	claiming `code`, a code grammar demoted to `data-document`, and a row claiming a
235	suffix the discovery table routes to another language each refuse with their own
236	typed cause. What is held equal to the `body-language-version` enum is therefore
237	the **`code` subset**, not the whole bundle — which accounts for all seven
238	languages instead of ignoring four.
239	
240	Claiming `declares`/`literal`/`control-flow` facts for a data format would
241	require a tokenisation law this kit does not publish, and inventing one would be
242	precisely the fabricated-semantics failure the syntax-only universe exists to
243	prevent. If the product later wants data-format syntax facts, it needs a
244	published tokenisation and `literalKind` law first; that is a bounded future
245	capability and this matrix does not promise it today.
246	
247	An unbundled language stays unrepresentable: `.py` has no bundled grammar, is
248	not in the descriptor vocabulary, and its files remain `unsupported-file` with
249	reason `no-bundled-grammar`.
250	
251	**The capability law binds facts and Coverage, not just descriptors.** Validating
252	a grammar bundle's declared `syntaxClass` constrains what a bundle may say about
253	itself; it does not constrain what a Run may claim. An earlier revision enforced
254	the registry only there, and full Runs consequently admitted a Markdown-anchored
255	`declares` fact, a **complete** empty `declares`/`clones` Coverage over a
256	data-only repository, and `references@resolved-binding` under a universe whose
257	own record declares `resolutionAttempted: false`. The registry is therefore
258	consulted at the two boundaries that decide what a Run asserts, and at neither
259	does it consult the claimed coverage value, the caller-declared class, or
260	whether facts happen to exist:
261	
262	- **Every admitted fact.** A `fact2` under a syntax universe is admissible only
263	  if **every one of its anchor paths** is read by a **selected** grammar whose
264	  registry capability set contains that `relation@rung`. The anchor is the file
265	  the body was actually read from, so a Markdown-anchored code fact refuses in a
266	  mixed repository exactly as it does in a data-only one
267	  (`SYNTAX_CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED_FACT`). **Inventory capabilities are exempt
268	  here as well as at the scope boundary below** — the exemption belongs to the
269	  *relation*, not to the boundary. An earlier revision wrote this bullet as an
270	  unconditional every-anchor rule and stated the exemption only in the scope
271	  bullet, so the two bullets contradicted each other: a literal implementer
272	  refused a `file@enumerated` fact for `tool/main.py` while the scope bullet had
273	  just promised that the same path's inventory Coverage was unconditionally
274	  `complete` — an inventoried file that is authoritatively absent. An inventory
275	  fact is not read by a grammar at all; it *is* the inventory row, the manifest
276	  declaration or the VCS observation, so there is no grammar for it to be gated
277	  on. (The relation registry's `anchorLaw` independently gives the inventory
278	  class **zero** anchors, so such a fact names no anchor path for this bullet to
279	  test either; the two laws agree and neither leans on the other.) The exemption
280	  is from grammar ownership **only**: the relation's snapshot joins, own-scope
281	  attribution and the anchor law all still bind, and no code fact becomes
282	  admissible because some other anchor in the Run sits on a supported path.
283	- **Every requested scope, including an empty view.** A `subject-scope` under a
284	  syntax universe is judged on its committed **examined extent** — the source
285	  inventory of the snapshot it names. **Inventory** capabilities
286	  (`file@enumerated`, `package@manifest-declared`, `vcs-change@vcs-reported`) are
287	  **always** available and are deliberately **not** grammar-gated: a snapshot
288	  inventories every file it contains, including ones no bundled grammar reads,
289	  and requiring a grammar per inventory row would silently narrow that promise.
290	  A **code** capability requires at least one path in that extent to be read by a
291	  selected `code` grammar. A capability no selected grammar bears is unavailable —
292	  which is every semantic rung and `unresolved-edge` under a syntax universe,
293	  exactly as the matrix already says.
294	
295	**A promised inventory capability represents every inventoried path, and a
296	`complete` inventory result may not hide an omitted one.** These are two halves
297	of one promise and the second was missing. `file@enumerated` is **total** over
298	the snapshot inventory: a snapshot inventories exactly the files it contains, so
299	every inventoried path has exactly one `file` fact, and over a **complete**
300	`file@enumerated` Coverage the predicate `exists file where path=P` is
301	authoritative. A complete result that retains no fact for an inventoried subject
302	therefore asserts that an inventoried file is absent, and that graph closed —
303	nothing derived the obligation, so nothing compared it. A `complete`
304	`file@enumerated` Coverage must now carry an admitted `file@enumerated` fact for
305	every one of its subjects that the snapshot inventory contains
306	(`COVERAGE_INVENTORY_TOTALITY_OMITS_PATH`), derived at Run closure from the
307	retained view's own facts and the retained inventory.
308	
309	**A fact discharges the obligation of the scope it actually belongs to.** The
310	match is on every coordinate the registry's `matchOn` lists — the four
311	`CoverageKeyV2` coordinates other than the commitment itself
312	(`relation`, `resolution`, `sourceUniverse`, `targetUniverse`) plus the owning
313	`snapshotId`. Matching relation and rung *alone* is not enough in a view carrying
314	more than one universe, and this is not hypothetical: the view-level fact/scope
315	join is **existential** — each fact need only agree with *some* scope on relation,
316	rung and both universes — so a TypeScript `file` fact is lawfully present in a
317	view that also carries a syntax-universe `file@enumerated` scope, and while the
318	match was two-coordinate it *paid that scope's missing-file obligation*. A
319	complete Run exhibited exactly that: two `complete` scopes over `a.ts`, only the
320	TypeScript fact, admitted. Totality is a claim about what **this** universe
321	examined, so it must be discharged by evidence produced in this universe; a fact
322	from another universe is a different interpretation of the same bytes, not the
323	same observation. The two-universe Run in which *each* scope carries its own fact
324	remains lawful and is retained as a positive control. `snapshotId` is listed
325	although Run closure already forces it on every fact and scope: this law reads one
326	scope's obligation out of a *shared* view, and a join that silently leans on an
327	invariant enforced elsewhere is the same implicit coupling that produced the
328	cross-universe defect.
329	
330	Two things the law deliberately does not require: a subject the snapshot does
331	**not** contain is owed nothing —
332	the host examined the question and the file is genuinely absent, which is the
333	one case a universal negative over inventory exists to serve — and an `unknown`
334	result carrying its disclosed deficiency is owed nothing, which keeps a
335	partially examined inventory representable rather than forcing a false
336	`complete`. `package@manifest-declared` and `vcs-change@vcs-reported` are **not**
337	total and owe nothing: most paths declare no package and most were not changed,
338	so their empty results are ordinary findings. Which relations owe totality is
339	stated in the relation registry (`coverageTotality`), where only `file` has a
340	row, and never inferred. This is the specific rule that identity §3's "partition
341	the claimed universe without overlaps or omissions" defers to: the **disjointness**
342	half is general, applies within the full owning
343	`(snapshotId, relation, resolution, sourceUniverse, targetUniverse)` tuple, and is
344	decided at retained Run closure against the registry's own
345	`coveragePartitionLaw`; the **omission** half is discharged only where this
346	registry carries a `coverageTotality` row. For the nine `symbol`-kind relations it
347	carries none, and the reason is the trust boundary stated below — symbol-to-file
348	attribution is not re-derivable from the retained Run — so no omission obligation
349	exists there and none is invented. Disjointness still applies to them, because it
350	asks a different question: not what was examined, but whether one interpretation
351	claimed a subject twice.
352	
353	**How many spans a fact cites is a registry law, not an implementer's choice.**
354	`fact.anchors` carried no `minItems`, and only `clones` ever stated a
355	cardinality, so every published predicate over the array — the `file` row's
356	`anchorPathField`, and the every-anchor rule above — was universally quantified
357	and therefore *vacuously true* at zero anchors. It neither permitted nor forbade
358	the unanchored spelling, and both spellings of one `file@enumerated` claim closed
359	a Run with different `fact2` identities. The relation registry now carries a
360	closed `anchorLaw` on every relation, in three classes: `source-text` (the nine
361	code relations) needs **at least one** span, because a code fact is read from
362	source text and an unanchored one names no file that could have been read;
363	`body-identity` (`clones`) is **exactly one**, unchanged; and `inventory`
364	(`file`, `package`, `vcs-change`) is **exactly zero**, because such a fact's
365	whole semantic input is its payload, which the relation's own snapshot joins
366	already bind. Zero is also the only cardinality *every* inventoried path can
367	satisfy — including a `vcs-change` whose `changeKind` is `deleted`, whose path is
368	by construction not in the snapshot and can carry no anchor at all. The
369	`source-text` class deliberately imposes **no additional relation-specific
370	maximum** and no canonical extent *beyond the common schema bounds* —
371	`fact.anchors` already carries `maxItems: 100000` and `uniqueItems`, and those
372	continue to apply to every relation; what the class declines is a per-relation
373	ceiling or a canonical span set, not the shared one. Which spans a producer cites
374	is a real statement about what it read, so two producers citing different spans
375	have produced different semantic descriptors and legitimately mint different
376	identities. Nothing here promises cross-provider anchor identity for code facts. Two things this also closes that the previous
377	wording did not: an unanchored *code* fact was refused only inside this
378	syntax-universe guard and closed a Run under a TypeScript or Rust universe, and
379	`anchorPathField` existed only on the `file` row, so a `package` fact anchored
380	into an unrelated file closed a Run. One law now covers every relation in every
381	universe (`FACT_ANCHOR_CARDINALITY`).
382	
383	An **unselected** grammar lends no capability: selection is committed in the
384	universe identity, so a bundle that ships a Rust grammar the universe did not
385	select cannot make `declares@syntactic` available for `.rs` files.
386	
387	**An unavailable request is disclosed, not answered, and never refused outright.**
388	The capability is retained and representable: the scope closes a Run and carries
389	`coverage: unknown` with `deficiency: language-tier-unsupported` and
390	`nativeCause: capability-missing` — both already in the existing vocabulary, and
391	mapped in §10. A **false `complete`** for an unavailable capability, a wrong or
392	null cause, and a wrong deficiency each refuse with their own reason
393	(`SYNTAX_CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED_SCOPE`, `…_CAUSE_MISMATCH`,
394	`…_DEFICIENCY_MISMATCH`). No syntax Run is made blanket-indeterminate to achieve
395	this: a data-grammar inventory Run and a code-grammar `declares`/`clones` Run
396	both still close with a genuine `complete` and no deficiency.
397	
398	This particular guard — the one decided by the **selected grammar rows** — is
399	**syntax-universe specific**. Every *semantic* capability of the TypeScript and
400	Rust universes is unchanged, including all five semantic relations, and the Rust
401	compilation-ownership guards are untouched — see the ownership disclosure law in
402	§10, whose prerequisite is now derived from the actual universe kind so that a
403	grammar-only clone scope, which has no compilation unit at all, owes no
404	compiler-ownership obligation.
405	
406	It is **not** the only scope-capability guard, and an earlier revision of this
407	paragraph read as if it were. A separate and weaker law, stated in §10 and
408	published as
409	`identity-schemas.v2.json#/x-opensip-digest-domains/scopeCapabilityLaw`, applies
410	to **any** universe whose dialect form is a closed suffix table — TypeScript and
411	the syntax universe both — and asks only whether a scoped path's own suffix
412	selects a variant in the table that universe published. For the syntax universe
413	that condition is strictly weaker than the grammar law above and is implied by
414	it, because the capability registry's `data-document` class law already states
415	that **no suffix of a data grammar appears in the syntax dialect table**. For
416	TypeScript it is the *only* such law, and it is what a `clones` scope over
417	`package.json` is now answered by. Which guard reaches a given scope first,
418	however, is decided by what each boundary can see, not by which law is stronger.
419	The suffix law needs nothing but the scope's own paths, so the native Coverage
420	producer boundary already applies it to the one case it can judge from a single
421	record — a `source-path` relation carrying a body-identity join, which is
422	`clones` — whenever the caller hands it the owning universe's dialect, as Run
423	closure does. Closure runs that producer admission **before** any of its own
424	prerequisites, so a false claim of complete Coverage for a `clones` scope over
425	a path no dialect table lists is refused there, as a producer-admission failure
426	naming the source variant, before the grammar guard. The grammar law is neither weakened nor reordered: among
427	closure's own prerequisites it is still applied ahead of the suffix backstop,
428	and it remains the sole owner, under its own refusal names, of everything a
429	suffix table cannot see — the `symbol` relations, the other syntax relations,
430	and the selection case where a path's suffix *is* in the table but no selected
431	grammar row owns it. An honestly disclosed unsupported scope still carries
432	`coverage: unknown` and the published `language-tier-unsupported` /
433	`capability-missing` pair. A false claim of complete Coverage is rejected; its
434	internal first-refusal name depends on which admission boundary detects it.
435	
436	**A scope is judged on ITS OWN extent where the published law supplies one.** The
437	relation registry states, per relation, what `subject-scope.subjects` identify
438	(`subjectKindLaw`). For a **`source-path`** relation — `clones`, `file`,
439	`vcs-change`, which bind their subject to a snapshot path through their registry
440	`snapshotJoins` `pathField` or, for `clones`, through the single `bodyIdentityJoin`
441	anchor — the subjects **are** the extent, and **every** named path must be
442	supported. So a `README.md`-scoped clone request is unavailable even in a mixed
443	snapshot that also contains `src/plain.rs`: an unrelated code file elsewhere does
444	not serve it, and a scope naming both cannot hide its unsupported part behind its
445	supported one.
446	
447	For a **`symbol`** relation the subjects are opaque `SubjectIdV1` values that the
448	retained record associates with **no** path. The enumerator's attribution of
449	symbols to files is **trusted** and is not re-derivable from the retained Run, so
450	the only answerable question is the coarser one — can this universe produce this
451	capability anywhere in the committed extent — and that is what is asked. Treating
452	a symbol identifier as a path would reject lawful code scopes, and inventing
453	symbol-to-path parsing would be fabricated evidence. This is a stated
454	trust-boundary limit, not an oversight, and a mixed-repository empty `declares`
455	scope therefore remains admissible.
456	
457	**Path support is decided by the SELECTED grammar ROWS and their own suffixes**,
458	not by the set of selected languages. The descriptor permits a row to own a
459	**subset** of its language's bundled suffixes, and two rows of one language may
460	own disjoint suffixes; admission requires only that a claimed suffix belong to
461	that language and that no suffix be claimed twice. A selected TypeScript row
462	owning `.ts` therefore establishes nothing about a `.tsx` path when no selected
463	row owns `.tsx`, and longest match runs over the union of the selected rows' own
464	suffixes so `.d.ts` still resolves through a row owning `.ts`. An unanchored code
465	fact is **not** vacuously supported: it names no file that could have been read.
466	
467	**`allowJs` and `checkJs` are not completeness claims** (feedback 11; primary
468	sources `typescriptlang.org/tsconfig/allowJs` and `/checkJs`, read 2026-09-06).
469	`allowJs` is a *program-membership* option: it admits JavaScript roots. `checkJs`
470	is a *diagnostics* option: it reports errors in JavaScript files and changes
471	nothing about what is resolved. Both are universe keys (they change PlanId);
472	neither gates a capability, and neither implies that resolution was attempted or
473	complete. Resolution completeness is asserted only by `CoverageResultV3` (§4.3).
474	The universe carries `jsAdmittedToProgram`, `jsDiagnosticsEnabled` and the
475	constant `resolutionCompletenessImplied=false` so no consumer can confuse them.
476	
477	Module systems inside `typescript-v2` are observed, not chosen: `import`/`export`
478	and `require()`/`module.exports` are both resolved by the pinned compiler under
479	`module=node16` semantics keyed by `package.json` `type`. A non-literal specifier
480	is an unresolved edge (§4.4), never a silent drop.

505	Limitations (closed ids; each is disclosed in Coverage, never hidden):
506	
507	- **L-JS1** synthesized options: `paths`/`baseUrl`/`rootDirs`/custom `types` are unknown; a specifier resolvable only through them is `unresolved-module-specifier`.
508	- **L-JS2** dynamic forms: computed member access, non-literal `require`/`import()`, indirect `eval`, reflective access and `any`-typed calls produce unresolved edges; resolution completeness for universal negatives is then `incomplete` (§4).
509	- **L-JS3** JavaScript types without annotation or JSDoc are `compiler-inferred` (§4.8). They are exact under the admitted universe and carry no probabilistic confidence; a rule pack that wants declared types uses `derivationPolicy=declared-only`.

511	- **L-RS2** dynamic dispatch and generics: `dyn Trait` calls resolve to the trait method declaration and are recorded as `trait-object-dynamic-dispatch` unresolved edges; generic bound calls as `generic-bound-dispatch`. Both count against resolution completeness for universal negatives.
512	- **L-RS3** non-prepared generated code: procedural-macro and build-script outputs are absent; each external proc-macro invocation site is a `macro-expansion-unavailable` edge and each package with a build script contributes `build-script-generated-unavailable`. `types@checked` on items whose type depends on such generated code is `unknown` with `input-closure-incomplete` (cause `generated-output-unavailable`). Declarative `macro_rules!` expansion is compiler-native and fully supported.
513	- **L-RS4** prepared mode: only inert `macro-expansion`, `build-script-directives` and `generated-file` rows are consumed (the last through the read-only virtual `OUT_DIR`, §3.6 PO-4); a site or owner without a matching, non-stale row falls back to L-RS3 behavior for that site.
514	- **L-FW1** entry points: `reachability` universal negatives need an origin set; without a recognized framework or explicit origins they are `resolution-incomplete` with class `entry-point-unrecognized` (§8).
515	- **L-CL1** cross-TS/JS candidates use the `tsjs-erasure-v1` syntax projection; bodies with runtime-significant TypeScript tokens are excluded; a candidate is never a fact, never semantic equivalence and never a deletion prerequisite (§6.4).

517	### 1.4 Mixed repositories and workspace units (R1)
518	
519	The v1 rule ("deepest root, then `Cargo.toml` > `tsconfig.json`") was wrong: in a
520	repository whose root holds both `Cargo.toml` and `package.json`/`tsconfig.json`
521	every TypeScript file fell into the Rust unit and silently left the TypeScript
522	program. Units are now **per language family and program membership**, and may
523	share a root.

525	**Reference discovery model** (`discover_units`, `assign_membership` in the model;
526	records `WorkspaceUnitV2`, `FileMembershipRowV1`, `UnitMembershipV1`). The root
527	discovery boundary and trust decision remain the security/foundation owners'
528	(DR-103); this contract defines what happens inside that boundary.

530	`WorkspaceUnitV2` (closed): `{unitOrdinal, rootPath, languageFamily: rust|tsjs|none,

530	`WorkspaceUnitV2` (closed): `{unitOrdinal, rootPath, languageFamily: rust|tsjs|none,
531	languageMode, unitKind: cargo-workspace|cargo-package|ts-program|js-program|syntax-only,
532	markerPath, markerSha256, recognizerId, recognizerVersion, provenance:
533	EXPLICIT|DISCOVERED|DEFAULTED, memberPackageRoots[]}`.

698	**The capability vocabulary, its authority and its spelling (CB4-SHOULD-2).**
699	`analysis-spec.requestedCapabilities[].capabilityId` was `$ref: Text` and enters
700	`PlanId` through `analysisSpecDigest`, and no document named the vocabulary it is
701	drawn from. Three spellings were consequently in live use in one release: the
702	reference default-selection corpus emitted `relation@rung`
703	(`clones@normalized-body-hash`), the foundation reference fixture emitted a bare
704	relation name (`references`), and the capability matrix publishes `inventory`,
705	`syntax`, `clones-fact`, `clones-near`, `clones-cross-tsjs`, `unresolved-edge`.
706	Two conforming hosts requesting the same analysis of the same unit therefore mint
707	different `analysisSpecDigest`s, different `PlanId`s and different `RunId`s, which
708	defeats independent replay across machines. The `languageMode` sibling was
709	already closed against a registered map at Run closure; the capability was not.
710	
711	- **Authority.** `native/native-capability-matrix.v2.json#/capabilities[].id`,
712	  closed at eleven members, with the law published beside it at
713	  `#/capabilityIdLaw`. The same vocabulary serves
714	  `product-configuration.analysis.capabilities`, whose item pattern
715	  `^[a-z][a-z0-9._:-]*$` already contained no `@` — so the `relation@rung`
716	  spelling was never admissible at the configuration layer and is now refused by
717	  shape at the analysis-spec layer too, before membership is consulted.
718	- **A capability id is not a `relation@rung`.** They are different concepts and
719	  are not equated. A capability is a *requestable unit of work* and may cover
720	  several relations (`inventory` covers `file@enumerated`,
721	  `package@manifest-declared` and `vcs-change@vcs-reported`; `syntax` covers the
722	  three syntactic rungs) or none at all (`clones-near` and `clones-cross-tsjs`
723	  are candidate-only and bear no fact relation). A `relation@rung` is a
724	  *fact/Coverage coordinate*: it is what `CoverageKeyV2`, the §1.3 table, the
725	  grammar-capability registry and the relation ladders speak. The bridge in both
726	  directions is the matrix's own `capabilities[].relations`, so an implementer
727	  never has to guess one from the other.
728	- **Mode applicability.** A request names a capability *and* a `languageMode`.
729	  The `(capability, mode)` cell must exist — the table is the complete product of
730	  the eleven capabilities and the six modes, so it always does for registered
731	  members — and its state must not be `NOT-SELECTED`, which means "outside D-371;
732	  no promise" and is an *unsatisfiable* request rather than a disclosable one.
733	  An `UNSUPPORTED-TYPED` cell is a different thing entirely: it **is**
734	  requestable and is answered with `unknown` plus its own named deficiency and
735	  cause, never refused. Today's three `NOT-SELECTED` cells are
736	  `clones-cross-tsjs` under `rust-cargo`, `rust-cargo-prepared` and `syntax-only`.
737	- **The release declaration registry.** Its *content* stays an authenticated
738	  input — which rows a release ships is not a contract constant — but its schema
739	  (`native-evidence.schemas.v2.json#/$defs/ReleaseCapabilityRegistryV1`, rows
740	  `{capabilityId, languageModes[]}`), its membership authority (`capabilityId` ∈
741	  the matrix ids; every mode registered with a cell that is not `NOT-SELECTED`),
742	  its canonical spelling and its binding to the Plan are normative. A duplicate
743	  `capabilityId` refuses rather than merging, because two rows declaring
744	  different applicable modes for one capability would leave default selection
745	  ambiguous.
746	- **The analysis-spec ownership tuple is unique (CB8-SHOULD-2).** The rule above
747	  is the *release declaration's*; the **request** had no analogue, and it needed
748	  one for exactly the same reason. Within one analysis spec,
749	  `(capabilityId, languageMode, workspaceRoot)` **names one cell of work for one
750	  unit**, and `required` is that cell's **attribute**, not part of its name. Two
751	  rows over one tuple disagreeing only on `required` were admitted by the schema —
752	  `uniqueItems` sees two *distinct* items — and by the per-row vocabulary
753	  admission, which judges each row alone; and both entered `analysisSpecDigest`
754	  and therefore the `PlanId`, so the contradiction was **committed** rather than
755	  transient. Requiredness decides whether a missing Coverage entry contributes
756	  `indeterminate`, so an undetermined value there is not cosmetic. Such a spec is
757	  **refused**: there is deliberately no last-wins, no order dependence and no
758	  merge of requiredness, and a caller states one value per cell or the record is
759	  refused. The same `capabilityId` on a **different** `workspaceRoot` or a
760	  different registered `languageMode` is a different cell and remains legal, and
761	  different capabilities on one unit remain legal. In an **explicitly supplied**
762	  spec a **byte-identical** duplicate row is a different defect and keeps its own
763	  earlier answer — `uniqueItems` and the canonical-set order law refuse it at
764	  `validate_foundation`, before this rule is reached — so on that path this rule
765	  owns only distinct rows over one tuple. On the **default-construction** path the
766	  guard described below runs first and reports byte-identical rows under this same
767	  key; both paths name the same tuple. The law is published in the record's owning schema
768	  (`foundation/identity-schemas.v2.json#/$defs/analysis-spec`,
769	  `x-opensip-uniqueness`) and enforced in `admit_requested_capabilities`, the one
770	  helper that **both** the pre-Plan analysis-spec boundary **and** retained Run
771	  closure call, so the two boundaries agree by construction. It is a *determinacy*
772	  law and therefore belongs in that shared helper, unlike the population
773	  **cardinality** bound, which is a pre-Plan request-selection concern and stays at
774	  the request boundary; §10 keeps that cardinality-first special route unchanged.
775	  Its internal key `native.requested-capability-duplicate-ownership-tuple` is
776	  registered in the §10 route registry as **origin-dependent** over the existing
777	  external-configuration / externally-supplied-spec / host-generated-internal-layer
778	  routes, and it adds **no** public `DomainDetailCode` member. Default construction
779	  reports the **same** key. The matrix-fixed default emits unique tuples, and two
780	  co-located units in one mode produce byte-identical rows that
781	  `default_capability_selection` refuses rather than silently deduplicating, so no
782	  requested analysis is lost. That guard runs **before** the analysis-spec boundary
783	  — `uniqueItems` would otherwise answer with a generic schema error restating the
784	  whole instance, the same reason the §10 cardinality guard precedes generic
785	  validation — and it names this registered key, not a private one. An earlier
786	  revision raised a bespoke `DUPLICATE_REQUESTED_CAPABILITY` there, which had **no**

788	  (`native.public-route-key-unregistered`), so this duplicate-selection refusal had no derivable

790	  host-generated route was written for exactly that call site. The refusal, its
791	  position and its non-deduplicating behaviour are unchanged; only the key it names

879	- **Which capabilities use which route.** A **fact-producing** capability keeps

881	  does not replace it. A **candidate-only** capability has no Coverage entry at

884	- **What an absence projects to, and what wins when two apply.** Neither case may

1219	| Rule | Statement |
1220	|---|---|
1221	| Fold | `fold(n)` is Unicode **Default Case Conversion `toLowercase(X)`**: the **full**, **non-tailored**, **context-sensitive** default lowercase mapping (Unicode Standard §3.13 / UAX #21). Reference implementation `native_evidence_model.v2.lib_name_fold` |
1222	| Mapping | `component(n) = "lib." + fold(n) + ".d.ts"`. Total, deterministic and **one-directional**: a selected name maps to exactly one component basename, and a component is never mapped back into a selected name |
1223	| Membership | for every `n` in `libSelection`, `component(n)` must be an element of the declared `component` set. A name whose component is absent refuses `native.native-context-lib-not-retained:<n>` — §10 route `request-rejected` (2) / `REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED`, before PlanId |
1224	| Equality | `{fold(n) : n ∈ libSelection}` must equal `{fold(m) : m ∈ honoredOptions.lib}`. `honoredOptions.lib` is required and non-empty in the closed resolved context, so this agreement always applies and is **not** weakened by the mapping. 1228	and only one of them is the one this admission performs, so it is named rather than approximated.

1233	| `U+039F U+03A3` (sigma in **final** position) | `U+03BF U+03C2` — the `Final_Sigma` condition | `U+03BF U+03C3` | `U+03BF U+03C3` |
1234	| `U+03A3 U+039F` (sigma **not** final) | `U+03C3 U+03BF` | `U+03C3 U+03BF` | `U+03C3 U+03BF` |
1235	| `U+00DF` LATIN SMALL LETTER SHARP S | `U+00DF` — unchanged | `U+00DF` | `U+0073 U+0073` |

1237	So `fold` is **not** `Simple_Lowercase_Mapping` (it expands, and it is position-dependent) and
1238	**not** `Case_Folding` (sharp s is unchanged). It is **non-tailored** — the root locale, with no
1239	Turkish/Azeri dotless-i and no Lithuanian tailoring — so the result must never depend on an ambient
1240	locale, an environment variable or a host language setting.
1241	
1242	**Version custody, and the portability consequence it does not hide.** The result of a default case
1243	conversion is determined by the Unicode case data the host carries, so `fold` is deterministic
1244	**given a case-data version**, and this design binds the reference derivation to one:
1245	`native_evidence_model.v2.UNICODE_CASE_DATA_VERSION`, currently **UCD 15.0.0**, the version the
1246	table above was measured against. Two hosts on different case data can fold the same name
1247	differently — for a code point unassigned in one of them (an unassigned code point folds to itself),
1248	or for one whose mapping changed between the versions — and because `libSelection` enters the
1249	context descriptor and therefore `PlanId`, that would be an admission divergence, not a cosmetic
1250	one. This contract does **not** claim the fold is invariant across every runtime. It requires the
1251	version to be a declared, checkable property rather than whatever the runtime happens to ship:
1252	`unicode_case_data_agreement()` reports the running version against the declared one so drift is
1253	disclosed instead of silently changing an outcome. Nothing here narrows the field to ASCII to
1254	sidestep the question — it is simply true that every `lib` name in the pinned compiler's own option
1255	vocabulary is ASCII, where all three operations above coincide, and that is a fact about the current
1256	vocabulary rather than a constraint on the value.
1257	
1258	**Custody: the two arrays answer different questions.** `libSelection` is the
1259	*configuration-facing* record of what the resolved options selected, and it is
1260	what the universe/config agreement is checked against.
1261	`standardLibraryComponentDigests` is the *tree-facing* **complete** declaration
1262	inventory of the retained stdlib closure — one row per `.d.ts` member with its
1263	raw digest, selected or not. So the selection never narrows the inventory and the
1264	inventory never adds a selected name: a missing inventory row refuses
1265	`native.native-context-stdlib-inventory-incomplete:<basename>`, and a tree in
1266	which two paths share a basename refuses
1267	`native.native-context-stdlib-tree-ambiguous-basename:<basename>` — the mapping's
1268	target would not be unique, and an arbitrary resolution is exactly what this
1269	refusal exists to prevent. The join reads **no other input**: not a
1270	caller-supplied map, not a filesystem lookup, not a compiler query, not the
1271	`typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot` value on its own.
1272	
1273	**No platform *field*, and the identity is still platform-specific.** Unlike the Rust context there
1274	is no `targetTriple`/`hostTriple`, because TypeScript *resolution semantics* — which specifiers
1275	resolve, which subjects are examined, what is checked — are platform-invariant by design (§1.1).
1276	That is a design selection of this contract, not a measurement, and it is **not** a claim that the
1277	identity is platform-invariant: `toolClosure.closureId` names a signed closure whose foundation
1278	`closure` descriptor includes `platform`, so the same source analysed with the platform-specific
1279	executables of two families mints two `nativeContextId`s — as it must, because different bytes ran
1280	(`typescript-context-identity-is-platform-specific-through-its-signed-tool-closure`).
1281	
1282	**Universe and Plan binding.** `typescript-v2.nativeContextId` is
1283	`H("native.context.typescript.v2", descriptor)` in the `Sha256Text` form. `PlanId` binds the
1284	same digest through `plan.nativeContextDigests`, which takes the **bare 64 hex** (§11, the
1285	foundation `plan` record's spelling) and is a canonical **set**: several units of one language
1286	legitimately share one context, and identical admitted contexts collapse to one member — that is
1287	deduplication of an identical descriptor, never of two different ones.
1288	
1289	`bind_typescript_universe(universe, admission, context)` refuses a universe whose `nativeContextId`
1290	this host did not mint (`native.universe-context-binding-mismatch`) and refuses a Rust-minted context
1291	outright (`native.native-context-language-mismatch`). The **retained context bytes are a required
1292	argument**: there is no context-free admit path, because an optional field-agreement check is not a
1293	rule — a caller that omitted it would obtain exactly the bypass this join exists to close. Omission
1294	is the typed refusal `native.universe-context-not-supplied`
1295	(`typescript-universe-bound-without-the-retained-context-refuses`); context bytes that do not hash to
1296	the admitted id refuse
1297	`native.universe-context-binding-mismatch:context-bytes-are-not-the-admitted-ones`.
1298	
1299	Given those bytes the two records must **agree where they overlap**: a matching `nativeContextId`
1300	commits to the context bytes, not to the universe's copy of them, so `languageMode`,
1301	`packageModuleType`, `allowJs`, `checkJs`, `lockfileKind`, `nodeModulesInReadSet`,
1302	`jsDiagnosticsEnabled`, `jsAdmittedToProgram`, `configOrigin`, the `extends`-graph emptiness and the
1303	synthesized-options presence are each checked against the context and refuse
1304	`native.universe-context-field-mismatch:<field>`.
1305	
1306	The context itself also has mandatory agreement rules. `moduleResolutionMode`
1307	equals `configProjection.honoredOptions.moduleResolution`. `libSelection` is
1308	strictly sorted by UTF-8 name bytes, contains no duplicate names under the
1309	published `fold`, and selects the same folded name set as the honored `lib` list
1310	— the same `fold` the component join above uses, and the only one this section
1311	defines; each record retains its specified order for hashing. The closed resolved context
1312	always materializes that nonempty list. When source configuration omits `lib`,
1313	the resolver supplies the pinned compiler's target-default library selection
1314	in both records; `null` is not an alternate resolved spelling.
1315	`standardLibraryComponentDigests`
1316	has strictly unique component keys in UTF-8 order. Context admission refuses any
1317	contradiction before its digest may enter Plan. In synthesized mode every value
1318	in `synthesizedOptions` equals the corresponding honored option, and an absent
1319	optional `jsx` means honored `jsx` is null. Presence alone is insufficient.
1320	These are semantic agreement checks in addition to closed schema validation;
1321	internal diagnostic suffixes remain operational refusal evidence, not new public
1322	DomainDetail codes.
1323	
1324	**Independent derivation (§9.5) applies to TypeScript exactly as to Rust.** The worker
1325	recomputes the context from its own sealed inputs; a differing byte is
1326	`Unavailable(native-context-mismatch)` before Analyze.

1357	`{schemaVersion:1, language:"rust", lockfileIdentity, packages:
1358	[DependencyPackageSourceV1…] sorted by (name, version, sourceId) UTF-8 bytes,

1361	`DependencyPackageSourceV1`:
1362	
1363	| Field | Rule |
1364	|---|---|
1365	| `name`, `version` | exact `[[package]]` values from `Cargo.lock` |
1366	| `sourceKind` | `registry \| git \| path \| vendored` |

1366	| `sourceKind` | `registry \| git \| path \| vendored` |
1367	| `sourceId` | exact `source` string from `Cargo.lock`, or `""` for path packages |
1368	| `lockChecksum` | 64-hex from the lock `checksum`, or `null` for git/path |
1369	| `fileManifestSha256` | H(`native.dependency-file-manifest.v1`, sorted `[{path, contentSha256, byteLength}]`) |
1370	| `fileCount`, `totalBytes` | exact uint64 |
1371	| `acquisition` | `{mode: in-snapshot-path \| in-snapshot-vendored \| imported-descriptor, descriptorId: ImportId\|null, vendorPath\|null}` |
1372	| `checksumVerification` | `tarball-matched \| self-consistent \| not-applicable \| mismatch` — `mismatch` refuses the whole set |

1375	Verification rules (feedback 3 corrected):
1376	
1377	- **DS-1 (registry, vendored tree)** A vendored directory carries a self-asserted
1378	  `.cargo-checksum.json`. Its `package` field equalling `lockChecksum` proves
1379	  nothing about the files: an attacker rewrites file contents and every `files`
1380	  entry while preserving `package`. The host therefore checks internal
1381	  consistency only (`package == lockChecksum`, every listed file's SHA-256
1382	  matches, no extra or missing files) and records `checksumVerification =
1383	  self-consistent`, `provenanceAssurance = declared`. Inconsistency is `mismatch`
1384	  and refuses the set. The reference model contains the mutation
1385	  (`ds1-mutation-preserving-package-checksum-stays-declared`): the mutated tree is
1386	  still admitted, and it is still *declared*, never authenticated.
1387	- **DS-2 (registry, tarball)** Only the exact `.crate` tarball whose SHA-256
1388	  equals `lockChecksum` yields `tarball-matched` / `registry-authenticated`. The
1389	  host extracts it deterministically into the CAS and computes the file manifest
1390	  itself. An extracted tree plus `.cargo-checksum.json` is DS-1.
1391	- **DS-3 (git)** The import supplies the checked-out tree for the exact `#rev`;
1392	  `not-applicable` / `declared`; the file manifest identity is the binding.
1393	- **DS-4 (path)** Path dependencies live in the snapshot; nothing is imported.
1394	- **DS-5 (no ambient reads)** `$CARGO_HOME/registry`, `~/.cargo`, `vendor/`
1395	  outside the snapshot, or any host path is read **only** as the explicit,
1396	  user-named source path of an import step (§7). Any acquisition mode outside the
1397	  closed set, or any fetch URL, refuses. No network fetch exists in any first-party
1398	  code path (design invariant, conformance-checked; not a confinement claim).
1399	- **DS-6 (completeness)** The set is complete for a target when every package
1400	  activated by `UnifiedFeaturesV1` is present with `checksumVerification ≠
1401	  mismatch`. An incomplete set is admitted with `completeness.incomplete` and
1402	  typed `input-closure-incomplete` Coverage for dependent crates; it never blocks
1403	  syntax analysis.
1404	
1405	`declared` provenance is disclosed wherever the package matters: in the Plan
1406	(through the set descriptor), in `AuthorizedExecutionV2.owners[].provenanceAssurance`,
1407	and in the pre-execution sentence (§5.2). Facts derived from declared sources are
1408	still Plan-bound Coverage inputs; the disclosure is what changes.

1411	
1412	The host stores admitted dependency sources in its content-addressed store keyed

1422	Primary source (`doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html`, read 2026-09-06):
1423	Cargo reads `.cargo/config.toml` (and legacy `.cargo/config`) from the current
1424	directory and **every ancestor**, plus `$CARGO_HOME/config.toml`, merging arrays;
1425	it also honors `CARGO_*` environment overrides and knobs that select executables
1426	(`build.rustc`, `build.rustc-wrapper`, `target.*.linker`, `target.*.runner`),
1427	credentials and network. Stock Cargo has no switch that disables ancestor
1428	discovery, and this contract does not claim `--config` replaces the stack.

1430	The first-party `opensip-cargo-adapter` therefore establishes a **verified
1431	ancestor carrier** (`CargoConfigProjectionV2`, all checked by
1432	`cargo_config_admission` in the model):
1433	
1434	- **CC-1** Before every Cargo invocation, every ancestor directory of the private
1435	  scratch root is checked for `.cargo/config.toml` and `.cargo/config`. Presence
1436	  is a refusal (`native.ambient-cargo-config`, exit 4), never a merge and never a

1439	  invocation; its `config.toml` is absent by construction.

1442	  presence of any is a refusal. Tool locations are passed as absolute closure
1443	  paths on the command line, not via environment.
1444	- **CC-4** Every selected tool digest equals its entry in `ToolClosureV1`.
1445	- **CC-5** Every `.cargo/config(.toml)` inside the snapshot (any directory, not
1446	  only the root) is replaced in the materialization by the single projected file;
1447	  the originals remain snapshot bytes for identity but are never read by Cargo.

1584	### 4.1 Two different completeness claims

1595	### 4.1a Producing recipe for `subjectScopeCommitment` (closed)
1596	
1597	The retained C-2 selector deferred computation and verification. This is the successor
1598	recipe; nothing about the historical artifact changes.
1599	
1600	**Recipe.** `subjectScopeCommitment` is the foundation **subject-scope** identity of the
1601	examined partition, re-spelled in the native `Sha256Text` text form:
1602	
1603	```
1604	scope2      = identity-and-evidence H("subject-scope", D)          -> "scope2:"  + hex
1605	commitment  = "sha256:" + the same 64 hex                          -> Sha256Text
1606	```
1607	
1608	where `D` is the closed foundation record
1609	`identity-schemas.v2.json#/$defs/subject-scope`
1610	`{schemaVersion: 2, snapshotId, sourceUniverse, targetUniverse, relation, resolution,
1611	enumeratorClosure, subjects}`.
1612	
1613	**Inputs, exactly, and where each comes from.** `snapshotId` is the admitted `snapshot2`.
1614	`relation`/`resolution` are the Coverage key's own relation and rung. `sourceUniverse` and
1615	`targetUniverse` are the bare 64-hex universe digests of the same key (§2, §11).
1616	`enumeratorClosure` is the `closure2` of the Plan-bound enumerator that produced the
1617	partition. `subjects` is the **complete** examined subject inventory that enumerator
1618	enumerated over that snapshot, a canonical set (foundation ordering, duplicates refuse
1619	rather than dedupe). **Encoding**: the foundation canonical encoder and `H` frame, imported,
1620	not restated. There is **no native `H` domain for this field**: one preimage, one digest,
1621	two admitted textual spellings (§11).
1622	
1623	**Join with `scope2`.** The commitment is the *identical* digest to the `scope2` the host
1624	binds into the `coverage2` descriptor (`coverage.scopeId`). It is therefore not a second
1625	commitment and cannot drift from the scope it names. Its purpose is that the Coverage
1626	*payload* — the bytes whose `payloadDigest` mints `coverage2` — carries the provider's
1627	in-band commitment to the partition it claims to have examined, which the host then checks
1628	against a value the provider never supplied.
1629	
1630	**Where it is produced and checked (`admit_coverage_result_v3`, the admitted native producer
1631	boundary).** For every `CoverageResultV3` a provider sends, before any `coverage2` exists:
1632	
1633	1. The host builds `D` from **its own** enumeration and mints `scope2`. A provider-supplied
1634	   commitment is never an input to this step.
1635	2. `key.relation`, `key.resolution`, `key.sourceUniverse`, `key.targetUniverse` must equal
1636	   `D`'s (`native.coverage-key-scope-mismatch:<field>`).
1637	3. `key.subjectScopeCommitment` must equal the computed commitment
1638	   (`native.subject-scope-commitment-mismatch`).
1639	4. `entry.examinedUniverse.subjectScopeCommitment` must equal the key's
1640	   (`native.examined-universe-commitment-mismatch`) and
1641	   `entry.examinedUniverse.subjectCount` must equal `len(D.subjects)`
1642	   (`native.examined-universe-subject-count-mismatch`). A provider that examined a narrower
1643	   partition than the host enumerated is detected here, and by nothing else.
1644	5. RC-2 (§4.3) is rechecked over the same partition.
1645	6. Only then is `coverage2` minted from `{schemaVersion: 2, scopeId, payloadSchemaDigest,
1646	   payloadDigest}`. `payloadSchemaDigest` is the raw SHA-256 of the **exact registered schema
1647	   DOCUMENT bytes** (§7.2). A caller may restate it but never choose it: a value that is not the
1648	   registered document's digest refuses `native.coverage-payload-schema-not-registered`
1649	   (`coverage-payload-schema-digest-a-caller-chose-is-refused`).

1651	Every refusal above is `PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION` (`operational-failed` 4) under the §10
1652	fault law: a worker that lies about its partition contributes no facts, no Coverage and no
1653	Run. This is not a Coverage deficiency; an admitted-but-incomplete input is (§10).

1655	**Coverage use (`coverage_view_use`).** A `view2` may name a `coverage2` only if that
1656	`coverage2` was admitted at the boundary above and its `scope2` is one of the view's own
1657	`scopeIds`. A hash-valid `coverage2` whose subject scope sits outside the evaluated view is
1658	refused exactly as hidden finding evidence is (identity §3), rather than joined silently.
1659	
1660	**No circularity.** `D` names the snapshot, the universes and the enumerator closure. A
1661	universe descriptor (§2) names its native context, tools and config projection; a native
1662	context names closures; none of them names a scope, a Coverage, a view, an evidence record
1663	or a Run. The derivation order is therefore total and acyclic: closures → native context →
1664	universe → `scope2` → commitment → Coverage payload → `coverage2` → `view2`. The foundation
1665	scope *descriptor* whose raw digest is `scopeDigest` (§1.4, workspace roots and path
