704	## 7. Explicitly authorized test execution (AR-08)
705	
706	Repository code execution is disabled by default. `opensip test run` (request class
707	`execution`) is admitted only when: the security unit admits a `RepoExecutionGrantV2`
708	with principal `P-TRUSTED-REPO`, execution class `test-runner`, bound to this
709	project, snapshot digest and the exact `argv` digest, expiry operation-end, never
710	inherited (`TEST.PRINCIPAL_NOT_ADMITTED` otherwise); CI uses a pre-existing policy
711	record (`TEST.INTERACTIVE_CONSENT_IN_CI`); `argv[0]` is a `LogicalPath` member of the
712	sealed snapshot or a member of the declared toolchain `closure2`
713	(`TEST.ARGV_NOT_IN_CLOSURE`); the working directory is the project root or a
714	`LogicalPath` inside it; the environment is constructed from an allowlist only, `PATH`
715	is never copied (`TEST.ENV_NOT_ALLOWLISTED`) and is set to the toolchain closure; and
716	the live tree still equals the `afterStep` snapshot. There is no shell string and no
717	interpolation anywhere in the schema.
718	
719	The step **discloses** and does not confine: `effects.network/subprocess/
720	filesystemWrite` are `DISCLOSURE-ONLY` unless the security unit's platform truth
721	table measures a primitive; a claimed enforcement without a measured primitive is
722	refused (`TEST.CONFINEMENT_CLAIM_REFUSED`). The mandatory sentence before spawn is
723	"Repository test command will run with your user authority. OpenSIP does not prevent
724	network access or other effects on this platform." Output is bounded and truncation
725	is recorded. The outcome is a `TestPayloadV1` wrapped as an `import2` of kind `test`
726	— evidence, never Coverage and never a verdict; a verdict may depend on it only
727	through a declared policy predicate. Imported independently prepared test results
728	are the supported alternative.

733	
734	`workflows/command-inventory.v1.json` is the candidate single inventory,
735	validated by `command-inventory.schema.json`; the checker refuses a command name
736	outside the closed enum and requires every golden to be reachable by the model.
737	
738	| Group | Commands |
739	|---|---|
740	| analysis | `opensip` (default: discovery + durable analyze), `analyze [--ephemeral] [--baseline]`, `fit` (advisory whole-repository report), `audit --baseline [--audit-profile] [--closure-bundle]`, `repair verify` |
741	| query | `recommend` (advisory next-step suggestions from discovery), `query OP`, `baseline show`, `policy show`, `policy test`, `candidates`, `inspect`, `review brief`, `repair preview` |
742	| mutation | `import`, `baseline adopt|export|upgrade`, `policy init`, `waive`, `review join`, `repair apply`, `repair recover`, `purge` |
743	| execution | `test run`, `native prepare` (both explicitly authorized) |
744	| lifecycle / serve / meta | `install`, `update`, `core update|repair|rollback`, trust/store commands, `doctor`, `agent serve`, `help`, `version`, `completion` |
745	
746	Only `policy init`, `waive`, `baseline adopt|export|upgrade` write tracked intent.
747	Advisory projections never offer SARIF or manufacture a Control verdict. `fit`
748	may run an authoritative analysis by default and then return an advisory report;
749	its underlying sealed Run retains its own verdict.
750	
751	**Renderers.** `human` v1, `json` v2 (the `CommandEnvelope` major 2 is the parity
752	reference), `sarif` v1 (analysis class only; results equal envelope findings
753	one-to-one, verdict/deficiency in run properties), `html` v1 (analysis and query;
754	static single file, no script-fetched data, shows resolution completeness and
755	disclosures), `agent` v1 (the JSON envelope plus `agentHints` that never alter a
756	parity field). Each command names its `parityFields`; every applicable renderer must
757	carry semantically equal values for them. Every advertised SARIF command (`default`,
758	`analyze`, `audit`, `repair-verify`) must declare the common fields `run-id`,
759	`verdict`, `required-coverage`, `deficiency`, `findings`, `termination-class` and
760	`retention-disclosure`; inventory admission refuses an omission. SARIF results
761	and run properties are taken from this same declared host projection, as are
762	human/JSON/HTML/agent values; no renderer reads an undeclared findings field or
763	substitutes null for a present verdict/deficiency. Audit adds its comparison
764	fields while preserving the current analysis result. Repair verification adds
765	applied/verified snapshot, snapshot-match, targets-remaining and net-new-findings
766	fields while preserving the fresh verification Run's findings and verdict.
767	An empty findings array is a real empty result; it is never inferred from a
768	missing projection field. Ephemeral analysis retains its existing no-Run rule:
769	`run-id` is explicitly null in the projection's non-authoritative case,
770	never a fabricated Run. Required-output failure still follows the law below.
771	The host projection must be total over the selected command's `parityFields`
772	before a renderer consumes it: every field has its schema-admitted value,
773	including an explicit null only where that field permits it. A missing field
774	or projection exception is a required-delivery operational fault, not an empty
775	result or a successful partial rendering: `operational-failed`, exit 4,
776	`faultCause=delivery-required`, `DELIVERY.REQUIRED_FAILED`. If a Run was already
777	committed, the termination retains its RunId and the after-commit detail below;
778	otherwise no RunId is invented. This classification also covers a pure reference
779	projection helper raising `KeyError`; that exception alone is not a public
780	termination. Actual host exception handling and renderer conformance remain
781	DR-G17/DR-G20 implementation qualification obligations.
782	Requesting a non-applicable format is
783	`REQUEST.UNKNOWN_OPTION` / `OUTPUT.FORMAT_NOT_APPLICABLE` (2). Failure of the selected
784	required renderer **after** a committed Run is `DELIVERY.REQUIRED_FAILED` (4) with
785	detail `DELIVERY.RENDERER_FAILED_AFTER_COMMIT`, the `runId` in the termination, and
786	no rewrite of the Run; failure of an optional export sink leaves `success`.
787	
788	**Query.** Twenty closed operations over one sealed view (`run2`, `snapshot2` or the
789	`latest` resolver, whose empty domain is `IDENTITY.UNKNOWN`), bounded page/items/depth/
790	visited nodes; `completeness=required` at a bound is `QUERY.COMPLETENESS_UNMET` (3),
791	best-effort is visible truncation with a cursor. Response context always carries
792	resolved view, Coverage, availability and `advisory` (true exactly for
793	`comparison.diff`, `candidate.list`, `inspection.show`, `review.brief`).
794	
795	**Doctor.** `opensip doctor` produces a typed report over closures, trust, store,
796	platform, project marker and the offline window. A produced report is `success` (0)
797	even when defects are found (detail `DOCTOR.DEFECTS_FOUND`); CI must inspect
798	`doctor.defectsFound`. Only an unproducible report is `HOST.IO_FAILURE` (4).
799	
800	A `doctor` report is a **different invocation** and therefore cannot deliver the
801	absences of an analysis invocation; `DoctorResult.defects[]` remains the
802	environment report it always was.
803	
804	**Release-availability absence rides the invocation that selected it.**
805	`CommandEnvelope.availability` (`CapabilityAvailabilityV1` =
806	`{stepCount, totalNoticeCount, steps[]}`, each step
807	`CapabilityAvailabilityStepV1` = `{stepId, noticeCount, notices[]}`) carries
808	every capability the selected product requires (native §1.4) that this release
809	did not declare available, for **every requested unit of every analysis step** —
810	a single-step command projects one step, and a named multi-step invocation
811	projects one entry per analysis step that made a selection. Each notice carries the complete ownership tuple in **typed
812	fields** — `capabilityId`, `languageMode`, `workspaceRoot` — with the existing
813	code `native.capability-unavailable` (a `const`, since the record declares one
814	condition); the tuple is never concatenated into a `subject`, because
815	`workspaceRoot` is a `UserInputPath` bounded at 4096 while `BoundedText` is 1024
816	and a truncated path would collapse two distinct units into one indistinguishable
817	notice. The collection is composed **per step** —
818	`{stepCount, totalNoticeCount, steps[≤64]}`, each step
819	`{stepId, noticeCount, notices[≤1024]}` — because 1024 is the
820	`analysis-spec.requestedCapabilities` bound and *not* an invocation-wide one: two
821	admitted selections of 1023 requests each compose 2046 notices, and no notice is
822	discarded to fit. A step that made no selection contributes no entry, a step that
823	found nothing absent contributes an empty entry, and the same tuple may recur in
824	different steps. Order is the selection's own.
825	
826	Envelope membership alone would **not** deliver it: `render` selects a command's
827	declared `parityFields`, so `capability-availability` is a declared parity field
828	of **every** `requestClass: analysis` command — `default`, `analyze`, `fit`,
829	`audit` and `repair-verify` — and every applicable renderer carries it: human,
830	JSON, SARIF, HTML and agent. Because it is *declared*, it is also **required**:
831	the host projection must be total over the command's parity fields, so a caller
832	whose invocation selected nothing supplies the explicit empty collection
833	(`{stepCount: 0, totalNoticeCount: 0, steps: []}`) rather than omitting the
834	field, and an omission is a required-delivery operational fault under the law
835	above, never a successful partial rendering.
836	
837	It is **advisory** — it terminates nothing, mints no Coverage, grants no Control
838	verdict or repair authority, and is never a clone `Candidate`, since published
839	Candidate records represent actual candidates. `AnalysisResult` is a closed union
840	and is not widened to carry it.
841	
842	**Failure envelopes carry their errors.** A `kind=failure` envelope requires a
843	nonempty `errors` array of `DomainDetail`; where a step termination's optional
844	`domainDetail` is absent, the composition in native §10 supplies the array from
845	the route's own detail code, and where it is present `errors` is exactly that
846	detail so the two surfaces never disagree. Before a Plan or Run exists no run
847	envelope is fabricated.

170	## 2. Separate report custody, semantic correctness and qualification
171	
172	The release gate has an authenticated invocation context before reading a
173	candidate report: exact host, provider/data closure, harness, matrix, corpus,
174	runner public key, runner identity, environment observation and platform profile.
175	The fresh qualificationRequestId (host RequestId grammar) also binds the
176	measurement campaign; an older report cannot satisfy a different campaign.
177	These come from the selected signed release closure and independently admitted
178	runner inventory. A report cannot supply or alter its own expected subject,
179	expected answers, trusted runner or performance baseline.
180	
181	The producer signs the exact report bytes through the qualification signature
182	frame: ASCII `opensip.qualification.report.2`, NUL, raw 32-byte host digest,
183	provider-closure digest, harness digest, and SHA256(report bytes), concatenated
184	in that order. Ed25519 keys are provisioned by the authenticated gate outside
185	the report. The gate verifies signature before parsing bounded report bytes.
186	The report's embedded schemaMajor is covered by the signature. Reusing this
187	signature frame for report schema 3 does not make schema 2 bytes schema 3.
188	
189	Authentication proves who supplied the observation; it does not prove the
190	machine executed correctly. The trusted first-party measurement harness,
191	runner observation path and gate are explicit TCB components. The harness must
192	execute the selected closure by verified handle, observe exit/EOF and normalized
193	actual results, and bind the exact measured environment. Product qualification
194	requires retained real measurements from every required lane; synthetic reports
195	are tagged reference-only and cannot be promoted. A producer cannot attest its
196	own unsupported hardware into the allowlist.
197	
198	The original G13 schema/validator remain frozen historical evidence. The new
199	`g13-result-schema.v5.json` and `g13-validator.v5.py` close the reproduced defects
200	for the historical 24-cell shape: independently pinned corpus oracles determine
201	expected atoms and counters, all subject digests join to trusted context, and
202	actual observations plus signature are required. Consistently relabeling every
203	candidate subject digest or zeroing both expected and actual counts now fails.
204	This adapter does not qualify the added JavaScript/Rust cells.
205	
206	## 3. Full-product matrix and report schema
207	
208	The current native matrix is
209	`native/native-capability-matrix.v2.json`. Expand each declared capability/mode
210	cell over its four platform families and each selected signed platform profile
211	from the security contract. A release inventory explicitly selects the
212	advertised supported cells; unsupported typed cells also receive refusal
213	conformance cases. No cell disappears because no runner happened to produce a
214	report. Syntax-only capability is further parameterized by the exact grammar
215	inventory; one grammar's result does not qualify another grammar.
216	
217	The full-product report schema is
218	`foundation/product-quality-report.schema.v3.json`; its gate reference is
219	`foundation/product-quality-validator.py`. A report covers exactly one trusted
220	runner/profile/environment and the required cell set for that lane. CellId is
221	`capability/mode/platform/profile/fixture`; each coordinate comes from the
222	reviewed matrix and corpus expansion, not from report labels. Every required
223	fixture names exact source/input bytes, selected capability/rung, expected
224	normalized observations, expected exit and independently chosen work/stress
225	bounds. Native reference scenarios supply semantic obligations; executable
226	native fixtures and their results must be admitted at implementation
227	qualification before a cell becomes QUALIFIED.
228	
229	The gate's expectedCells is constructed from the verified matrix/corpus and
230	release selection by the first-party gate. It cannot be supplied as a CLI JSON
231	argument, copied out of report fields or recomputed from candidate answers.
232	Expected observation atoms have closed fields `kind`, `subject`, `value` (all
233	strings); `value` is the schema-defined normalized scalar or canonical JSON
234	text for structured payloads. The admitted fixture's normalizer and schema
235	are part of its pinned harness closure. Report atoms sort by canonical bytes,
236	are unique, and must equal the independent oracle exactly. Counts and
237	correctness are calculated by the gate; they are absent from the submitted
238	schema. Duplicate cells/observations, wrong cell sets, wrong exit or substituted
239	answers cannot be hidden by a reported PASS flag because no such flag is read.
240	
241	Each benchmark records 3 warmups followed by 7 measured runs in that order,
242	with positive integer elapsed nanoseconds and peak RSS bytes. The gate calculates median
243	elapsed time and maximum RSS. For an existing baseline the limits are 1.20×
244	median time and 1.25× peak RSS, using checked wide-integer cross multiplication (never wrapping), plus the
245	fixture's independently reviewed absolute bounds. A new supported cell needs
246	an explicitly reviewed initial baseline and absolute budget; absence is not a
247	zero or automatic pass. The two baseline measurements must be both present
248	or both null. A null pair admits an initial-measurement report but never qualifies
249	a release-selected cell; reviewed initial baseline promotion is a separate gate act. Baseline host/provider/harness, fixture, environment and
250	platform profile must be compatible by the release gate's signed inventory;
251	changing the measuring subject cannot silently reuse an unrelated baseline.
252	Cold-start and retained-evidence workloads are separate fixtures, so warmup
253	cannot conceal startup or storage regressions. The old reference adapter
254	retains its historical hardware/performance baseline semantics unchanged.
255	
256	A well-formed authenticated report may report a failing observation. Report
257	admission and release qualification are separate: admission verifies custody,
258	shape and joins; qualification requires every selected cell's correctness and
259	performance to pass on every required profile lane. Missing, unavailable or
260	failed lanes block promotion. The release gate also requires lifecycle,
261	security, output parity and recovery gates; G13 alone never authorizes release.
262	
263	## 4. Reference evidence and implementation obligations
264	
265	`foundation/check-foundation.py` retains the original integer and G13
266	counterexamples, valid controls, exact canonical byte vectors and actual
267	Ed25519 signature verification with temporary test keys. The reference invokes
268	the local OpenSSL executable solely to exercise cryptography; production uses
269	the authenticated first-party implementation, never ambient tool discovery.
270	`foundation/check-identity.py` independently replays a bounded finite-relation
271	fixture and exercises identity, proof tampering, retention and crash-state
272	joins. It explicitly discloses its trusted evaluator callback and in-memory
273	carrier scope; it is not a general native interpreter or a durability proof.
274	The full-product report checks exercise a separate TS/JS/Rust-shaped cell set,
275	forged subject/corpus/answers, missing lanes and false performance claims.
276	
277	Reports record every scenario, source pins and limits. Independent review reads
278	semantics and executes adversarial controls; source hashes establish the
279	reviewed bytes, not correctness. Legacy self-reporting checker claims and their
280	observability escapes do not enter product evaluation authority. The corrected
281	product uses explicit admitted data plus trusted pure evaluation; an adversarial
282	program sharing the verifier's process is not claimed to be contained by Python
283	introspection. Native measurements, independent implementer reproduction and
284	supported-platform qualification remain the concrete pre-release gates.
285	
286	Discovery observations are folded into the trusted `defaults` layer by the host
287	before the reference Config2 resolver runs; their recognizer identity and path
288	provenance remain in the discovery record. The reference resolver does not scan
289	frameworks. A missing profile is `CONFIG_PROFILE_MISSING`; an unknown profile is
290	`CONFIG_PROFILE_UNREGISTERED`. Both pack and waiver IDs require registry admission.
291	
292	## 5. Complete product-boundary successor (DR-117)
293	
294	D-371/D-372 prospectively replace P-1/P-2/G3 only as enumerated here. These are the seven dispositions required by architecture file02, “Current V1 product boundary and required successors”; the historical enumeration and preview acceptance keep their original scope.
295	
296	1. **Marketplace/catalog and governance depth:** the selected product has one signed first-party component/recipe/schema registry. It has no public marketplace, third-party publisher admission or ecosystem governance promise. Unknown contributions refuse through the closed registry; declaring an id does not establish trust.
297	2. **External lifecycle parity and discovery:** supported first-party components receive the common installation, update, rollback, offline, doctor and removal contracts. Repository/framework discovery selects applicable admitted capabilities; it is not an external service and cannot install or execute discovered code. Third-party lifecycle parity is outside the selected scope, not a partially specified admission mode.
298	3. **Contribution roles beyond narrow/data-only:** first-party native providers may produce typed facts/Coverage and prepared input imports. Signed first-party declarative recipes/profiles may select host-owned steps. Only the host constructs findings, evaluates policy/verdict, owns persistence, finalization, rendering and termination. A component cannot acquire those powers by declaring a root command or emitting an output record.
299	4. **Untrusted native or WASM admission and enforcement:** neither is admitted in this product. No process/WASM boundary is claimed as a sandbox. Separately authorized repository-code preparation/tests are the explicit trusted-code principal of security S10, with the actual platform disclosure/enforcement matrix and revocation/cleanup rules. They do not open an untrusted plugin admission path. G09/G21/G29/G30 must exercise these refusal and authority boundaries; a synthetic fixture is not enforcement evidence.
300	5. **Imperative contributions, probes, project hooks and root commands:** arbitrary imperative contributions/project hooks/root-parser extensions are not admitted. The closed host command inventory owns every command. Named first-party repair, test, preparation and doctor operations have their exact explicit authorization and effect contracts; a recipe/profile cannot bypass them. Metadata discovery/help/recommend do not run repository hooks or probes. Consent to one executable step never becomes general command or persistence authority.
301	6. **Network-granted analysis and egress defaults:** ordinary analysis/discovery are offline; there is no implicit index refresh, download, telemetry or required egress. Explicit trust refresh/offline import and explicitly required export delivery have their named host lifecycle/output semantics. Repository-code effects are disclosed/admitted by their actual trusted-code grant; they are never silently reclassified as confined analysis. Required delivery failure can fail the invocation without changing a committed Run's assurance.
302	7. **G3 physical substrate:** the selected substrate is a signed Rust distribution core/semantic host, pure first-party evaluator, supervised native TS/JS and Rust components, and the signed offline assets and verified storage mechanics required for the selected authoritative profile. This replaces the prototype's lockstep Node/npm train and the preview's narrow command/provider set. The default product profile is authoritative-capable; an explicitly selected management-only installation is not an authoritative closure and refuses analysis until the required signed closure is separately installed through an authorized lifecycle operation. Missing assets never trigger ambient downloads or a weaker analyzer. Every physical dependency, including compiler/runtime/standard-library/LLVM/storage assets actually used, belongs to the admitted closure/TCB inventory and its packaging/offline/quality gates.
303	
304	The selected exclusions are D-371's credentials, third-party ecosystem, untrusted contributions and TUI exclusions; this section introduces no new scope cut. Product measurements remain required by the named release gates. This is a complete boundary selection now, not a promise that future implementation will choose these policies.
305

1	# Security and lifecycle: boundaries, time, trust, platforms, migration, concurrency
2	
3	Standing: proposed product successor authored by Claude (security unit) for
4	independent Codex review and D-372 application. It is NOT self-accepted. It
5	addresses AR-03, AR-04, AR-05, AR-06, AR-14 and the offline/doctor part of
6	AR-16, the nine items of Codex's intermediate review of the earlier draft, and
7	the CHANGES_REQUIRED items of Codex's review of the final chapter (handoff
8	`reviews/security-fix-handoff.v2.md`: S3 units, S4.5 counters and freshness,
9	S9.1 root schema 2 / profile-set binding, S10 grant V2 and S10.1 repair
10	authorization, S7 one-writer refinement and backup custody).
11	Reference evidence: [security/](../../../coop/design-corrections/security/)
12	(model, closed schemas, cases, checker, report, source pins). Reference checks
13	are design evidence over synthetic fixtures; they are not OS measurement,
14	cryptographic verification or product qualification. Every boolean signature or
15	OS observation consumed by the model is a stated TCB assumption.
16	
17	## S1. Authority, applicability and superseded selectors
18	
19	The first-party host is the only authority for discovery, trust time, root
20	chain acceptance, revocation, platform admission, migration and leases. Content
21	identity never proves custody. A signed document proves only that its signer
22	signed those bytes; whether the document is admitted is decided by the rules
23	below, evaluated at the host's trust instant.
24	
25	Prospectively replaced selectors (historical bytes stay immutable):
26	
27	| Reviewed source | Selector | Disposition |
28	|---|---|---|
29	| security v8 §4.2 and `security_unit_lib_v8.evaluation_time` | write-ahead `evalHighWater = max(recorded, wall, lastAccepted)` before evaluation | replaced by S4 (plausibility refusal before evaluation; floor written equals evaluated instant) |
30	| security v8 §4.8 `doctor_trust_report` | report-only evaluation | retained; S4 adds that report-only returns no actionable write fields and no challenge |
31	| security v8 §5.5 | restore keeps floors; no floor recovery | retained; S4.5 adds the only lawful floor-lowering act |
32	| security v8 §5.4 fence/lease handoff | one operation lease, non-blocking | refined by S7 (three lease modes, five-level lock order) |
33	| security v8 §8.3–8.7 | one measured profile per platform class | replaced by S8 (population with two tiers, four lanes) |
34	| host foundation v2 §§1–3 discovery | nearest-ancestor `opensip.json` walk to `/` | replaced by S3 |
35	| compatibility matrix v5 S-STATE/S-CTRL/S-SCHEMA | closed major one, no bridge | retained for stage 1; S9 is the explicit stage-2 successor |
36	| journal-record.schema v8 | GRANT/RA/ICI/RCI/ICO/RCO/REV/CLN/AUD | retained; schema-2 records add SEAL and `postimageSha256` (S6) |
37	
38	Unchanged inherited constants: 24 h future tolerance, 90 d revocation freshness
39	and catalog expiry, 365 d root expiry, expiry boundaries (`expired iff tEval >=
40	expiresAt`; `stale iff tEval > issuedAt + 90 d`). No D9 class, code or exit is
41	minted; every refusal maps to an existing D9 v1.14 code (table in S12).
42	
43	## S2. Two canonical profiles, never mixed
44	
45	Signed security metadata (root, catalog, revocation, journal records, recovery
46	challenge and epoch, platform profile population) stays under
47	`opensip-metadata-canonical.1`: NFC-required strings, i64 integers, its own
48	domain-framed digests. Product data (discovery provenance, decision records,
49	execution grants, everything with a `schemaVersion`) uses the foundation
50	canonicalizer of identity-and-evidence §3: no normalization, integers to
51	2^64-1, `H(domain, descriptor)`. A decoder for one profile never admits the
52	other's documents. The reference checker demonstrates the separation with a
53	decomposed string and an integer above i64 (sweep `metadata-nfc-profile-and-
54	product-profile-never-mixed`).
55	
56	## S3. Discovery and custody (AR-03)
57	
58	Discovery is deterministic over lstat/ACL results obtained through O_NOFOLLOW
59	handles: no environment variable, no `PATH`, no `HOME` (the account home comes
60	from the account database). Output is the closed `DiscoveryProvenanceV1`.
61	
62	The disposable discovery instrument accepts only its named host-observation keys:
63	required `invokingUid`, `accountHome`, `cwd`, `fs`; optional `ci`,
64	`trustProjectOwner`, `authorizedGroupIds`, `explicitProject`, `explicitResolved`,
65	`explicitJoins`, `configWorkspaceRoots`. Unknown/missing keys or wrong outer
66	scalar/container types are `DISCOVERY_OBSERVATION_SHAPE` instrument errors,
67	not public D9 input refusals. Boolean observations are exact booleans and uid/gid
68	observations are nonnegative integers, never coerced strings or booleans. The
69	lstat/ACL map remains a synthetic trusted observation, not proof of native custody.
70	Public invocation/configuration admission still precedes this host-only seam.
71	
72	**Custody of a directory** passes only if: it is a real directory (no symlink);
73	owner is the invoking uid or root; mode has no other-write bit; mode has no
74	group-write bit unless the directory's gid is in the explicitly authorized set;
75	no ACL write grant (POSIX ACL on Linux, `acl_get_fd_np` on macOS) to any
76	principal other than the invoker, root, or an authorized group; and the ACL was
77	readable. Mode bits alone never establish exclusion. **Custody of a config
78	file** adds: regular file, link count 1, at most 4 MiB. Group authorization
79	exists only through an explicit `--trust-group <gid>` invocation argument and
80	is recorded in provenance; configuration cannot grant it. `--trust-project-owner`
81	waives only the owner check and only with an explicit `--project` path.
82	
83	**Walk rule.** With `--project`, the resolved path is examined exactly once
84	(symlink resolution recorded). Otherwise, from the launch directory upward, at
85	most 256 levels: a custody failure at the launch directory refuses
86	(`PROJECT.ROOT_CUSTODY_REFUSED`); a custody failure at an ancestor is a
87	boundary and that ancestor is never examined for a config. At each passing
88	directory the config, if present, is custody-checked (failure refuses
89	`CONFIG.CUSTODY_REFUSED`; it is never skipped) and selects that directory
90	(`mode: config`). Boundaries after a directory without config, in precedence:
91	VCS marker (`.git`, `.hg`, `.svn`, `.jj`), account home, filesystem root, mount
92	change. A VCS boundary selects **that repository root** (`mode: vcs-default`),
93	never the launch directory, so default scope does not change with launch
94	directory. Home, root, mount and custody boundaries without any candidate
95	select the launch directory (`mode: cwd-default`).
96	
97	**Nested config is a deliberate project boundary (decided; ADV-3).** A config
98	file found below a VCS root is an author-declared project root and wins for
99	launches inside it; the walk never continues above a config. The enclosing
100	VCS-root project treats that directory exactly like a nested repository: it is
101	recorded in `nestedProjects`, automatic discovery never enters it (excluded
102	unit reason `INSIDE_NESTED_PROJECT`), and an explicit join crossing into it
103	refuses `PROJECT.EXPLICIT_PATH_INVALID` (`JOIN_CROSSES_NESTED_PROJECT`). Scope
104	therefore depends only on which project a launch is inside, never on which
105	directory of one project. The alternative (VCS root always wins) was rejected
106	because it would silently ignore a config the repository author placed. Cases
107	`nested-config-inside-a-vcs-root-*` and
108	`explicit-join-crossing-into-a-nested-project-refuses`.
109	
110	**VCS data.** A `.git` indirection file (`gitdir:`) is data: its target is
111	recorded and never followed by discovery; VCS digests for the snapshot are the
112	identity unit's concern and read only inside custody.
113	
114	**Authority roots versus workspace units.** Two different things are
115	distinguished. A *project authority/custody root* is the selected root: one
116	custody domain, one ProjectId, one lease namespace. Repositories nested under
117	it are other custody roots: they are recorded as `nestedRepositories`, never
118	entered, and reachable only by their own `--project`; a join that crosses into
119	one refuses `PROJECT.EXPLICIT_PATH_INVALID` (`JOIN_CROSSES_NESTED_REPOSITORY`).
120	A *language workspace unit* is a directory inside the admitted root that
121	carries a manifest marker: `Cargo.toml`, `package.json`, `tsconfig.json` or
122	`jsconfig.json` (markers may co-locate; a unit lists all its markers). Units are
123	discovered **automatically** for the zero-config full product, with precedence:
124	
125	| Source | Provenance `unitSource` | Custody failure |
126	|---|---|---|
127	| repeatable CLI `--workspace-root PATH` overrides | `explicit-joins` | refuses (explicit intent) |
128	| admitted Config2 `discovery.workspaceRoots` (foundation product-configuration schema v2) | `config-workspace-roots` | refuses |
129	| marker scan of the admitted root | `automatic` | unit excluded, recorded in `excludedUnits` with the reason |
130	
131	An explicit source suppresses automatic discovery. Every directory from the
132	root to a unit must pass directory custody and stay inside the root (no
133	absolute, `.`, `..`, backslash or NUL segments); every marker file must pass
134	file custody. A manifest is **data**: discovery records its presence and later
135	readers parse it as data only, never running scripts, hooks, plugins or
136	workspace globs and never writing source.
137	
138	**One shared discovery rule (MUST-3).** The zero-config rule is stated once, in
139	`docs/coop/design-corrections/discovery-defaults.py`, and consumed by this
140	instrument and by the native unit instrument (native §1.4); neither restates
141	it. Before any custody walk, automatic discovery prunes, by **exact path
142	segment** (never substring): dependency trees (a segment `node_modules`), VCS
143	trees (`.git`, `.hg`, `.svn`, `.jj`) and Cargo build output (a segment
144	`target` whose parent directory holds `Cargo.toml`, an actual Cargo root; a
145	source directory merely called `target`, such as `packages/target` or
146	`src/target`, is ordinary source). A pruned tree yields no unit, no marker,
147	no custody walk and no program member; its anchor is recorded **once** in
148	`prunedTrees` with the number of markers it hid, so 4200 installed package
149	manifests are one record, never 4200 units. A `Cargo.toml` inside a pruned
150	tree does not create a Cargo root. First-party unit directories are capped at
151	4096; exceeding the cap refuses typed `PROJECT.WORKSPACE_UNIT_LIMIT` (D9
152	`REQUEST.UNSATISFIABLE`, detail `WORKSPACE_UNIT_LIMIT:<n>><cap>`) with no
153	truncation; installed dependencies never count toward it (checker sweep
154	`discovery-prunes-installed-dependencies-and-refuses-real-cap-typed`: 4200
155	installed manifests admit with one unit; 4200 first-party directories refuse;
156	exactly 4096 admit).
157	
158	**Explicit roots are exact roots.** CLI `--workspace-root` and Config2
159	`discovery.workspaceRoots` values are normalized by the shared
160	`normalize_explicit_root`: `.` alone denotes the admitted project root
161	(identity-and-evidence §3 sentinel; internal root ``, the same value the native
162	instrument uses), one trailing `/` is dropped from a CLI value (a Config2 value
163	spelled with a trailing `/` is refused earlier by the foundation
164	product-configuration resolver's logical-path grammar and never reaches either
165	instrument; case
166	`cli-workspace-root-with-trailing-slash-normalizes-like-the-native-instrument-config2-refuses-it-earlier`),
167	and any other empty, `.`, `..`,
168	absolute, backslash or NUL segment is `JOIN_PATH_GRAMMAR`. An explicit root
169	inside a pruned tree refuses `JOIN_INSIDE_PRUNED_TREE:<reason>:<anchor>`. An
170	explicit root **without a language marker** is admitted here for custody (unit
171	recorded with `markers: []`, warning
172	`EXPLICIT_ROOT_WITHOUT_LANGUAGE_MARKER:<path>`) and refused by the language-unit
173	layer as `CONFIG.INVALID` / `native.explicit-root-without-marker` (native
174	§1.4); the invocation terminates typed with this provenance retained. That is
175	the selected behaviour: custody admission and language-unit existence are two
176	different facts, and neither instrument normalizes the same value differently.
177	Custody-excluded units are explicit unknown required scope, not a successful
178	empty scope; later syntax scanners cannot read their uncustodied source. There is
179	no config "project list" and no duplicate `--project` implicit multi-project
180	mode: `discovery.workspaceRoots` is the only configuration carrier. Cases
181	`installed-dependencies-and-cargo-build-output-are-pruned-by-segment-*`,
182	`config2-workspace-root-dot-*`, `explicit-root-*`.
183	
184	**Pruned trees and the read set (A-5).** "No custody walk" for a pruned tree
185	means discovery neither enumerates units in it nor walks its directories for
186	custody. Bytes a language program later reads from such a tree (a TypeScript
187	resolution reading `node_modules`, native §2.2/§9.4) enter the snapshot read
188	set through the identity unit's snapshot custody, are Plan-bound like every
189	other read-set byte, and are never a discovery unit; they are not exempt from
190	custody, they are custody-checked by the snapshot reader instead of the
191	discovery walk.
192	
193	**Admitted boundary inventory for the language-unit instrument (decided; post-reset
194	v2 N-1/P3).** The native unit instrument (native §1.4 U-8) never re-derives a
195	project boundary from caller input. After an `ACCEPT`, the host calls
196	`boundary_inventory(result)`, which converts this instrument's absolute custody
197	locators (`nestedRepositories`, `nestedProjects`, custody/depth `excludedUnits`,
198	`prunedTrees`) into the closed `AdmittedBoundaryInventoryV1` of relative scope
199	paths under the selected root (shared implementation
200	`discovery-defaults.boundary_inventory_from_provenance`; one boundary prefix
201	rule `classify_boundary` is used by both instruments). The host passes that
202	record unchanged to native `discover_units`, `assign_membership` and
203	`unit_scope_descriptor`; the native instrument then yields exactly this
204	instrument's unit set, excludes every marker directory and file at or below a
205	boundary, refuses an explicit root crossing one (`native.explicit-root-crosses-boundary`,
206	the counterpart of `JOIN_CROSSES_NESTED_*`) and enters every boundary anchor
207	into the Plan scope descriptor's `excludedPathPrefixes`. An inventory whose
208	pruned trees do not equal the ones the native instrument derives from the same
209	marker inventory is refused (`native.boundary-inventory-mismatch`): a
210	caller-supplied ignore list is never proof of boundary completeness. A `REFUSE`
211	result exports nothing. Cases `boundary-inventory-*`; checker sweep
212	`admitted-boundary-inventory-joins-security-discovery-and-native-unit-discovery`
213	runs the P3 fixture through both instruments. **The integration join is implemented, not owed:**
214	`integration-host-model.py` `admit_repository_discovery` composes `discovery` →
215	`boundary_inventory_from_provenance` → native `discover_units`/`assign_membership`/
216	`unit_scope_descriptor`, and `check-integration.py` asserts it
217	(`host-nested-boundaries-admitted-once`, `-no-native-units`, `-no-source-capture`,
218	`-plan-visible`, `host-native-inventory-substitution-refused`,
219	`host-launch-inside-nested-config-selects-that-project`, plus
220	`security-native-shared-unit-roots` and `security-native-shared-pruned-trees`).
221	
222	Native custody obligation (qualification, not modelled): ACL reads, O_NOFOLLOW
223	handle reuse for the later read, and re-check of `st_dev/st_ino` between lstat
224	and open. A change between them is a refusal, not a retry.
225	
226	### S3.1 Backup custody before the first source-derived write
227	
228	Identity-and-evidence §5 (TM V17) is joined here as an admission step, not a
229	prose promise: when the storage root is classified **detected backup-managed**
230	(`BACKED_UP`), the first source-derived write needs an explicit choice, in this
231	order: `--ephemeral`; `--allow-backup-custody` for this invocation; or an
232	already-admitted host storage-policy record. CI never prompts and refuses
233	`REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED` / `storage.backup-choice-required`. **UNKNOWN
234	admits** with a mandatory disclosure (`unknown-disclosed`): it is never
235	rendered as not-backed-up and it never requires the choice (fixture
236	`unknown-backup-status-is-not-not-backed-up`, identity §5, the inventory flag
237	joins and the S13 addendum agree). The choice writes no policy file and changes
238	no root identity (ProjectId, namespace locator). Sync/shared/upload storage
239	classifications are independent checks. Reference `storage_write_admission`;
240	fixture `storage-write-cases.v1.json`.
241	
242	## S4. Trust time (AR-04)
243	
244	Definitions. `evalHighWater` (floor F): highest instant at which a decision
245	evaluation was made. `lastAccepted` (L): issue time of the newest accepted
246	signed document; required whenever F exists. **Admitted time evidence** A =
247	max(L, accepted witness time, presented root issue time), where a witness is
248	the newest issue time of a presented payload whose signature already verified
249	and which is not older than L. The wall clock is untrusted.

## S10. Execution principal `repository-code`

Principal classes: `first-party`, `repository-code`, `imported-artifact`.
Repository execution is disabled by default. The display names are aliases of
one foundation semantic-grant principal kind: workflow `P-TRUSTED-REPO` and
native `repository-code` both map to `trusted-repository-code`
(identity-schemas.v2 `semantic-grant`). Two identities are kept apart: the
foundation `semanticGrantDigest` (semantic projection inside plan2: principal
kind, closure, owner-source digest, operations, scope; no nonce, expiry or
consent) and the operational `securityGrantRef` =
`H("security.repo-execution-grant.v2", grant)` under the product canonicalizer
(this record). The workflow `TestExecutionStepParams.authorizationRef` and the
native `AuthorizedExecutionV2.authorization` both reference the operational
identity.

A `RepoExecutionGrantV2` (supersedes the never-accepted V1 draft, retained in
the bundle as superseded) is admitted only when: schema 2; principal
`repository-code`, `semanticPrincipalKind` `trusted-repository-code`;
projectId, snapshotId (`snapshot2:`) and argv digest equal the invocation's;
execution class in {build-script, proc-macro, test-runner}; **owners** (≤ 64,
unique) each bind `{ownerKey, source, ownerFileManifestSha256}` where `source`
is `snapshot-member` (validated against the sealed snapshot's owner manifests)
or `dependency-closure-member` (validated against the **sealed
`DependencySourceSetV1`**, whose id must equal `dependencySourceSetId`) — so
build scripts and proc-macros of external crates are grantable exactly when
they are in the sealed closure, never from an ambient registry or vendor
directory; `ownerSourceDigest` equals the host-computed owner-set digest; the
**runner** is a
member of the sealed first-party tool closure (`toolClosureId`, `closure2:`;
bundled cargo/rustc/linker/test runner) for build-script and proc-macro, or a
tool-closure member or sealed snapshot member for test-runner — there is no
system cargo, rustc, linker or shell fallback; `platformId` is one of the four
S8 machine platform ids (a display alias refuses); every effect value (`subprocess`, `filesystemWrite`,
`network`, `environment`) **equals** the security owner's platform truth
table entry (currently `DISCLOSURE-ONLY`, `DISCLOSURE-ONLY`, `DISCLOSURE-ONLY`,
`ENFORCED-BY-CONSTRUCTION` on all four platforms; a stronger or weaker claim
refuses). Those four effect *names* are copied from four of the seven closed
permission **tokens** in `permission-truth-tables.v9.json`, and the
correspondence — `subprocess`→`PT-PROC-EXEC-DECLARED`,
`filesystemWrite`→`PT-FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE`, `network`→`PT-NET-EGRESS`,
`environment`→`PT-ENV-READ`, with the values read from the `child-process`
execution mode these owners run in — is tabulated in native §5.2. Two limits
carry with it: `PT-FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE` names the **host's own state store**, so
neither the token nor a grant over it confers authority over the repository
filesystem — its `DISCLOSURE-ONLY` value states that nothing prevents writes
anywhere, since the code holds the invoking user's ambient authority; and
`PT-HOST-EFFECT-BROKERED`, the one token whose value is
`ENFORCED-AT-HOST-BROKER`, is deliberately projected by no effect name, because
repository code here is not routed through a host broker. Confinement remains
never claimed; authorization is `interactive-explicit` (never in CI) or
`policy-record` with a record id; the grant's `ci` flag is a real boolean equal
to the invocation's; the project policy admits the principal; expiry is
operation-end; not inherited. The native contract copies these effect values
into `AuthorizedExecutionV2.effects` and its `owners[]` are this grant's
owners; the workflow contract's `consentSource` (`pre-existing-policy` |
`interactive-consent`) maps to `policy-record` | `interactive-explicit`, and
its `argv0Source` maps to `runner`. Revocation of a running grant is the S6
path; confinement is never claimed.

**Operational admission precedes any Plan (decided; SHOULD-2).** A grant
authorizes one *operational* step: native preparation (build-script /
proc-macro owners, workflow `native prepare`) or a workflow test-execution step
(test-runner). Preparation runs before the analysis Plan that will consume its
outputs exists, and a test-execution step has no Plan at all (workflows §1/§7),
so **no Plan semantic-grant projection is an admission input** of
`admit_repo_execution_grant`; a ctx projection supplied beside the grant is not
read (`a-ctx-projection-is-never-consulted-not-an-authority-condition`), and a
host must not fabricate one from the grant. The bindings that hold every grant
are the ones listed above: project, snapshot, argv digest, execution class,
owners (preparation classes), runner, tool closure, platform and truth-table
effects, consent, `ci`, expiry, non-inheritance, and the S6 live boundaries
during the step. For a test-runner grant `owners` is `[]` and
`ownerSourceDigest` is the digest of the canonical empty owner array
(`4f53cda1…2b945`): canonical empty-set bookkeeping that keeps the record
shape uniform and binds nothing; the runner is bound by `runner` +
`toolClosureId`/snapshot membership + `argvDigest`
(`test-runner-grant-admits-with-no-plan-*`,
`test-runner-runner-outside-both-sealed-sets-refuses-although-the-empty-owner-digest-matches`).

The Plan-time join is separate and later. `semantic_projection_for_grants`
lists the `trusted-repository-code` principals (`{kind, closureId,
ownerSourceDigest}`) of the **preparation** grants whose prepared outputs an
analysis consumes; a test-runner grant contributes nothing, because its
evidence enters a Plan only as an `import2` payload whose wrapper and
test-execution step receipt retain the operational `securityGrantRef`. When the
analysis is admitted, `admit_plan_execution_projection(planPrincipals,

plan2 semantic-grant projects exactly those principals
(`PLAN.EXECUTION_PRINCIPAL_NOT_PROJECTED:<digest>` /
`PLAN.PROJECTED_PRINCIPAL_WITHOUT_GRANT:<digest>`), refuses any
`trusted-repository-code` principal under `imported-inert` or `none` (prepared
availability never implies this host held a grant), and refuses a test-runner
grant offered as a consumed grant (`PLAN.TEST_RUNNER_HAS_NO_PLAN`). The
projection comes from the Plan and the grants from the step receipts; they must
agree, and neither is derived from the other. D9: `REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED`
(request-rejected 2). Records `SemanticProjectionV1`,
`ExecutionProjectionAdmissionV1`; cases `plan-*`,
`semantic-projection-for-grants-*`. **Implemented, not owed:**
`integration-host-model.py` derives the Plan requirement through
`semantic_projection_for_grants(grants)` and `check-integration.py` drops

`imported-inert-does-not-infer-local-grant`, `test-runner-is-operational-not-a-plan-principal`,

Repair apply is host-brokered **first-party** source mutation: the host writes
postimages it computed from a signed recipe closure under the EXCLUSIVE lease.
No repository code runs. Its authorization is therefore a separate record,
`RepairApplyAuthorizationV1` (product data; identity
`H("security.repair-apply-authorization.v1", record)` is the workflow
`RepairApplyParams.authorizationRef`), admitted only when: projectId,

invocation's; the live tree still equals the base snapshot
(`AUTHZ.SOURCE_MOVED`); `recipeClosureId` (`closure2:`) equals the recipe in
the rehashed repair plan (`AUTHZ.RECIPE_CLOSURE_MISMATCH`) and is positively
admitted under current signed-closure trust (`AUTHZ.RECIPE_CLOSURE_NOT_ADMITTED`).
Absence from the revocation set is insufficient. Revocation refuses first
(`AUTHZ.RECIPE_CLOSURE_REVOKED`, D9
`EXTENSION.ADMISSION_REJECTED`); consent is `interactive-explicit` (never in

expiry operation-end; `leaseMode` `EXCLUSIVE`; `repositoryExecution` is the
constant `false` and cannot be set. Live revocation: every brokered write
passes the S6 authority checkpoint; a revoked recipe closure at any checkpoint
is `REV(trust-revoked)` with postimage-checked rollback and the workflow's
`FAILED_ROLLED_BACK` / `RECOVERY_BLOCKED` states. Reference
`admit_repair_authorization`; fixture `repair-authorization-cases.v1.json`.

### S12.1 Projecting a refusal onto the one closed public detail vocabulary

A public termination carries exactly one `domainDetail` = `{code, remedy, subject?}`, and `code` is a
member of the single closed registry (`design-corrections/public-detail-registry.v1.json`, mirrored by
`workflows/schemas/common.schema.json#/$defs/DomainDetailCode`). This section states the projection
this unit's refusals take, so that "detail" in the prose above is never ambiguous between a registry
member and free subject text. Reference `public_detail` / `public_details`, record
`PublicDetailProjectionV1`, fixture `public-detail-cases.v1.json`, sweep
`public-domain-details-are-a-closed-set-with-a-bounded-pending-registration-gap`.

1. **Base code, then subject.** The base code is everything before the **first** colon; everything
   after it is subject data. `ROOT.ROLE_SET:1` is code `ROOT.ROLE_SET`, subject `1`.
2. **A registered detail wins over the enclosing refusal.** When a refusal carries a `detail` whose
   base code is a registry member, that is the public code. This is why the 38 `ROOT.*` document
   defects are public codes instead of collapsing into one `PAYLOAD-NOT-ADMISSIBLE`, and it is
   exactly why `ENVELOPE.*` and `PROFILE_SET.*` belong in the registry: they occupy the same position
   in `admit_profile_set_envelope` that `ROOT.*` occupies in `admit_root_document`, and S9.1 names
   them normatively as `detail`.
3. **Otherwise the refusal supplies the code and the whole detail is subject text.** This is the
   existing reading for `RECOVERY.REFUSED` (`CHALLENGE_EXPIRED`, `COUNTER_MISMATCH:<k>`,
   `ISSUED_TOO_OLD_FOR_WALL`, …), for `CONFIG.CUSTODY_REFUSED` (`SYMLINK`, `WRITABLE_BY_OTHERS`, …)
   and for `PROJECT.EXPLICIT_PATH_INVALID` (`JOIN_PATH_GRAMMAR`, `JOIN_INSIDE_PRUNED_TREE`, …). Those
   sub-details are deliberately **not** registry members; registering them would create a second
   public vocabulary for the same events.
4. **The vocabulary is closed, not a prefix rule.** The unit declares the exact set it may emit
   (`SECURITY_PUBLIC_DETAIL_CODES`, 191 members). A detail whose base code lies inside one of the
   eight families this unit publishes (`AUTHZ.`, `ENVELOPE.`, `GRANT.`, `NT-TCB-`, `PLAN.`,
   `PROFILE_SET.`, `ROOT.`, `TRANSITION.`) but outside that set **refuses**; there is no open
   `PROFILE_SET.*` wildcard.
5. **The D9 branch comes from the refusal, never from the detail.** Naming a defect more precisely
   never changes its termination branch. `PROFILE_SET.NO_TR_PROFILE_ROLE` therefore travels under
   `ROOT.SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED` → `REQUEST.SCHEMA_MAJOR_UNSUPPORTED` exactly as S9.1 says, while every
   other `PROFILE_SET.*`/`ENVELOPE.*` defect travels under `PAYLOAD-NOT-ADMISSIBLE` →
   `EXTENSION.ADMISSION_REJECTED`. Members of the three document-admission families
   (`ROOT.`, `ENVELOPE.`, `PROFILE_SET.`) that the D9 table does not name individually take that same

   exception is `AUTHZ.RECIPE_CLOSURE_REVOKED`, which is an admission rejection while every other
   `AUTHZ.*` detail of the same admission is a precondition failure.
6. **Internal decision keys are aliased, never published.**
   `RF-6:AUTHORIZATION.GRANT_NOT_CURRENT`, the S6 linearization trace's spelling for a request
   refused after revocation, is an internal alias of the registered
   `TRUST.COMPONENT_REVOKED_DURING_OPERATION`.

"""Constructors for complete positive Run descriptor graphs.

Every observation a provider, compiler, filesystem or OS would make is a
SYNTHETIC TRUSTED OBSERVATION supplied here.  None of it is measurement, and
none of it is native enforcement proof.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib

import canon as K
import kit
import native as N
from evaluator import address_nodes, replay, EvalView
from store import Store, Refusal, split_id

PROJECT_ID = "prj1-" + "3f" * 32


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# closures (synthetic signed components)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def make_closure(store, kind, files, semantic_version, protocol_major=3,
                 platform="linux-x86_64-gnu"):
    tree = []
    for path, data in sorted(files.items()):
        d = store.put_blob(data)
        tree.append({"path": path, "sha256": d, "bytes": len(data)})
    tree.sort(key=lambda r: r["path"].encode("utf-8"))
    manifest_body = K.C({"kind": kind, "semanticVersion": semantic_version,
                         "platform": platform, "tree": tree})
    manifest_digest = store.put_blob(manifest_body)
    desc = {"schemaVersion": 2, "kind": kind, "manifestDigest": manifest_digest,
            "tree": tree, "semanticVersion": semantic_version,
            "protocolMajor": protocol_major, "platform": platform}
    cid = store.put_identity("closure", desc)
    return cid, desc


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# snapshot
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def make_snapshot(store, files: dict[str, bytes], scope_descriptor, config,
                  vcs_kind="git", commit="a" * 40, dirty=False):
    inventory = []
    for path, data in files.items():
        d = store.put_blob(data)
        inventory.append({"path": path, "sha256": d, "bytes": len(data)})
    inventory.sort(key=lambda r: r["path"].encode("utf-8"))
    inv_digest = store.put_record(inventory)
    vcs = {"schemaVersion": 2, "kind": vcs_kind,
           "commitId": None if vcs_kind == "none" else commit,
           "dirty": dirty, "sourceInventoryDigest": inv_digest}
    vcs_digest = store.put_record(vcs)
    scope_digest = store.put_record(scope_descriptor)
    config_digest = store.put_record(config)
    desc = {"schemaVersion": 2, "projectId": PROJECT_ID,
            "sourceInventory": inventory, "resolvedConfigDigest": config_digest,
            "scopeDigest": scope_digest, "vcsDigest": vcs_digest}
    sid = store.put_identity("snapshot", desc)
    return sid, desc, inventory


def default_config(capabilities, budget_limit=100000, profile="default"):
    return {
        "analysis": {"profileId": profile,
                     "capabilities": sorted(capabilities),
                     "budget": {"unit": "work-units", "limit": budget_limit}},
        "components": {}, "discovery": {}, "policy": {}, "evidence": {},
    }


def scope_descriptor(roots, prefixes=(), excluded=()):
    return {"schemaVersion": 2,
            "workspaceRoots": sorted(set(roots), key=lambda s: s.encode()),
            "pathPrefixes": sorted(set(prefixes), key=lambda s: s.encode()),
            "excludedPathPrefixes": sorted(set(excluded), key=lambda s: s.encode())}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# capability manifest (CVE1, admitted under capability-manifest-domains.v2)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def capability_manifest(relations, ladders, extra=None):
    """A minimal CapabilityManifestV1-shaped record over the two relation
    registries capability-manifest-domains.v2 declares."""
    man = {"schemaVersion": 1,
           "relations": sorted(relations),
           "relationLadders": {r: list(ladders[r]) for r in sorted(relations)}}
    if extra:
        man.update(extra)
    return man


def commit_capability_manifest(store, manifest):
    """ADM-ORDER is applied before encoding; CVE1 then encodes the committed
    bytes and the identity is SHA256(domain || 00 || committedBytes)."""
    admit_capability_manifest(manifest)
    committed = K.cve1(manifest)
    digest = store.put_blob(committed)
    return K.capability_manifest_id(committed), digest, committed


def admit_capability_manifest(manifest):
    """The four inherited gates, in their inherited order (identity S3, native S11)."""
    reg = kit.doc("capability-domains")
    domains = _find_value_domains(reg)
    _adm_type(manifest)
    _adm_closed(manifest)
    _adm_domain(manifest, domains)
    _adm_order(manifest)


def _find_value_domains(reg):
    out = {}

    def walk(node):
        if isinstance(node, dict):
            for k, v in node.items():
                if k in ("RELATION-DOMAIN-V2", "RELATION-LADDER-DOMAIN-V2"):
                    out[k] = v
                walk(v)
        elif isinstance(node, list):
            for v in node:
                walk(v)

    walk(reg)
    return out


def _adm_type(node):
    """ADM-TYPE: exact JSON type before any content comparison."""
    if isinstance(node, bool):
        return
    if isinstance(node, int):
        if isinstance(node, bool):
            raise Refusal("ADM-TYPE", "boolean offered as integer")
        return
    if node is None or isinstance(node, str):
        return
    if isinstance(node, list):
        for v in node:
            _adm_type(v)
        return
    if isinstance(node, dict):
        for k, v in node.items():
            if not isinstance(k, str):
                raise Refusal("ADM-TYPE", "non-string key")
            _adm_type(v)
        return
    raise Refusal("ADM-TYPE", type(node).__name__)


def _adm_closed(node, path="$"):
    """ADM-CLOSED: every reachable RECORD is closed; a map is not a record."""
    known = {
        "$": {"schemaVersion", "relations", "relationLadders"},
    }
    if path in known and isinstance(node, dict):
        extra = set(node) - known[path]
        if extra:
            raise Refusal("ADM-CLOSED", f"{path}: {sorted(extra)}")
    return


def _adm_domain(manifest, domains):
    """ADM-DOMAIN: every scalar bound to a named registry or declared open."""
    rd = domains.get("RELATION-DOMAIN-V2")
    ld = domains.get("RELATION-LADDER-DOMAIN-V2")
    members = _members(rd)
    for r in manifest["relations"]:
        if r not in members:
            raise Refusal("ADM-DOMAIN", f"relation {r} not in RELATION-DOMAIN-V2")
    ladders = (ld or {}).get("ladders") or {}
    for r, ladder in manifest["relationLadders"].items():
        want = ladders.get(r)
        if want is None:
            raise Refusal("ADM-DOMAIN", f"no ladder domain row for {r}")
        for rung in ladder:
            if rung not in want:
                raise Refusal("ADM-DOMAIN", f"{r}@{rung} is a rung of another relation")


def _members(dom):
    if dom is None:
        raise Refusal("ADM-DOMAIN", "RELATION-DOMAIN-V2 absent")
    for key in ("members", "values", "relations"):
        if key in dom:
            v = dom[key]
            return set(v) if not isinstance(v, dict) else set(v)
    raise Refusal("ADM-DOMAIN", "no member list on RELATION-DOMAIN-V2")


def _adm_order(manifest):
    """ADM-ORDER: every ordered collection already in its declared order."""
    rel = manifest["relations"]
    if rel != sorted(rel, key=lambda s: s.encode("utf-8")) or len(set(rel)) != len(rel):
        raise Refusal("ADM-ORDER", "relations")
    ladders = kit.RELATION_REGISTRY["relations"]
    for r, ladder in manifest["relationLadders"].items():
        want = ladders[r]["ladder"] if r in ladders else None
        if want is not None and ladder != want:
            raise Refusal("ADM-ORDER", f"ladder {r} is not the authority's order")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# plan / views / evidence / seal / run
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def make_plan(store, snapshot_id, snapshot, capability_manifest_id,
              capability_bytes_digest, semantic_closures, analysis_spec,
              native_context_digests, policy_digest, waiver_digest,
              semantic_grant_digest, budget, import_ids=()):
    spec_digest = store.put_record(analysis_spec)
    desc = {"schemaVersion": 2, "snapshotId": snapshot_id,
            "capabilityManifestId": capability_manifest_id,
            "semanticClosures": sorted(set(semantic_closures), key=K.C),
            "analysisSpecDigest": spec_digest,
            "resolvedConfigDigest": snapshot["resolvedConfigDigest"],
            "nativeContextDigests": sorted(set(native_context_digests), key=K.C),
            "importIds": sorted(set(import_ids), key=K.C),
            "policyDigest": policy_digest, "waiverDigest": waiver_digest,
            "scopeDigest": snapshot["scopeDigest"], "budget": budget,
            "semanticGrantDigest": semantic_grant_digest,
            "capabilityManifestBytesDigest": capability_bytes_digest}
    return store.put_identity("plan", desc), desc


def make_scope(store, snapshot_id, source_universe, target_universe, relation,
               rung, enumerator_closure, subjects):
    desc = {"schemaVersion": 2, "snapshotId": snapshot_id,
            "sourceUniverse": source_universe, "targetUniverse": target_universe,
            "relation": relation, "resolution": rung,
            "enumeratorClosure": enumerator_closure,
            "subjects": sorted(set(subjects), key=K.C)}
    return store.put_identity("subject-scope", desc), desc


def make_fact(store, snapshot_id, relation, rung, source_universe,
              target_universe, producer_closure, payload, anchors,
              confidence=1000000):
    payload_digest = store.put_record(payload)
    desc = {"schemaVersion": 2, "snapshotId": snapshot_id, "relation": relation,
            "resolution": rung, "sourceUniverse": source_universe,
            "targetUniverse": target_universe, "producerClosure": producer_closure,
            "payloadSchemaDigest": kit.doc_digest("relation"),
            "payloadDigest": payload_digest,
            "anchors": sorted(anchors, key=K.C),
            "confidenceMillionths": confidence}
    return store.put_identity("fact", desc), desc


def coverage_entry(relation, rung, commitment, subject_count, *,
                   coverage="complete", state=None, attempted=None,
                   examined_exhaustive=True, stage_terminal="complete",
                   edge_count=0, edge_classes=(), deficiency=None,
                   native_cause=None, derivation_kinds=(), confidence=1000000,
                   closed_world=None):
    resolved = rung in kit.RESOLVED_RUNGS
    if state is None:
        state = "complete" if resolved else "not-applicable"
    if attempted is None:
        attempted = resolved and state in ("complete", "incomplete", "partial")
    if not resolved:
        attempted, edge_count, edge_classes, stage_terminal = \
            False, 0, (), stage_terminal
    cw = closed_world or {
        "exportsClosed": "closed", "entryPointsRecognized": "all",
        "nonliteralLoading": "none", "externalConsumers": "none-declared",
        "dynamicDispatch": "not-applicable", "reasons": [],
        "deadCodeRepairEligible": True}
    return {"relation": relation, "resolution": rung, "coverage": coverage,
            "examinedUniverse": {"subjectScopeCommitment": commitment,

            "resolutionCompleteness": {
                "state": state, "attempted": attempted,
                "examinedExhaustive": examined_exhaustive,
                "stageTerminal": stage_terminal,
                "unresolvedEdgeCount": edge_count,
                "unresolvedEdgeClasses": sorted(edge_classes)},
            "closedWorld": cw,
            "derivationKinds": sorted(derivation_kinds),
            "confidenceMillionths": confidence,
            "deficiency": deficiency, "nativeCause": native_cause}


def make_coverage(store, scope_id, scope, entry):
    payload = {"schemaVersion": 3,
               "key": {"relation": scope["relation"], "resolution": scope["resolution"],
                       "sourceUniverse": scope["sourceUniverse"],
                       "targetUniverse": scope["targetUniverse"],
                       "subjectScopeCommitment": "sha256:" + split_id(scope_id, "scope2")},

"""Assemble a complete Run graph from admitted parts, then replay + close it."""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib

import build as B
import canon as K
import closure as CL
import kit
from evaluator import EvalView, replay
from store import split_id


def semantic_grant(store, scope_digest, operations=("read-source", "native-analysis"),
                   principals=None):
    g = {"schemaVersion": 2, "projectId": B.PROJECT_ID,
         "principals": principals or [
             {"kind": "first-party", "closureId": "closure2:" + "0" * 64,
              "ownerSourceDigest": None}],
         "analysisOperations": sorted(set(operations), key=lambda s: s.encode()),
         "scopeDigest": scope_digest}
    return store.put_record(g), g


def compile_program(policy, policy_digest):
    return {"schemaVersion": 1, "policyDigest": policy_digest,
            "rules": [{"ruleId": r["ruleId"], "ruleProgramRef": r["ruleProgramRef"],
                       "emitWhen": r["emitWhen"]} for r in policy["rules"]]}


def finish_run(store, *, plan_id, plan, snapshot_id, views, view_ids, scopes,
               facts, coverages, policy, policy_digest, waivers, rule_program,
               evaluator_closure_id, detector_closure_id, exec_plan_id,
               universe_language, capability_manifest_id, tamper=None):
    """Replay the evaluator, then mint proof/findings/evidence/seal/run."""
    rp_digest = store.put_record(rule_program)
    view = EvalView(facts=facts, scopes=scopes, coverages=coverages,
                    universe_language=universe_language)
    result = replay(policy, rule_program, rp_digest, view, waivers)

    # retain the witness and program-predicate preimages
    for w in result["witnesses"].values():
        store.put_record(w)
    for pp in result["programPredicates"].values():
        store.put_record(pp)

    eval_inputs = []
    for vid in view_ids:
        eval_inputs.append({"domain": "view", "digest": split_id(vid, "view2")})
    for cid in coverages:
        eval_inputs.append({"domain": "coverage", "digest": split_id(cid, "coverage2")})
    eval_inputs.append({"domain": "rule-program", "digest": rp_digest})
    eval_inputs.append({"domain": "policy", "digest": policy_digest})
    eval_inputs.sort(key=K.C)

    # findings
    finding_ids = []
    findings_out = []
    for f in result["findings"]:
        rule = next(r for r in policy["rules"] if r["ruleId"] == f["ruleId"])
        tokens = [f"path:{f['subject']}", f"rule:{f['ruleId']}"]
        discriminator = hashlib.sha256(K.C(tokens)).hexdigest()
        store.put_blob(K.C(tokens))
        fp = {"schemaVersion": 2,
              "ruleStableId": rule["ruleProgramRef"]["ruleStableId"],
              "detectorSemanticsMajor": rule["ruleProgramRef"]["semanticsMajor"],
              "subjectKey": {"language": "typescript", "kind": "file",
                             "logicalPath": f["subject"],
                             "qualifiedName": f["subject"],
                             "discriminator": discriminator},
              "relatedSubjectKeys": []}
        fp_id = store.put_identity("finding-fingerprint", fp)
        params = {"schemaVersion": 2, "messageCode": rule.get("messageCode", "cb9.finding"),
                  "parameters": {"subject": f["subject"]}}
        pdigest = store.put_record(params)
        witness_refs = sorted(
            [{"domain": "predicate-witness", "digest": p["witnessDigest"]}
             for p in result["predicateProofs"]
             if p["ruleId"] == f["ruleId"] and p["subjectId"] == f["subject"]
             and p["predicateId"] == "p"], key=K.C)
        fin = {"schemaVersion": 2, "fingerprint": fp_id,
               "ruleClosure": detector_closure_id, "subjectId": f["subject"],
               "messageCode": params["messageCode"], "parameterDigest": pdigest,
               "severity": rule["severity"], "evidenceRefs": witness_refs}
        fid = store.put_identity("finding", fin)
        finding_ids.append(fid)
        findings_out.append(fin)

    verdict = result["verdict"]
    if tamper == "verdict":
        verdict = {"fail": "pass", "pass": "fail",
                   "indeterminate": "pass"}[result["verdict"]]

    proof = {"schemaVersion": 2, "planId": plan_id, "executionPlanId": exec_plan_id,
             "evaluatorClosure": evaluator_closure_id,
             "ruleProgramDigest": rp_digest,
             "evaluationInputRefs": eval_inputs,
             "predicateProofs": result["predicateProofs"],
             "findingIds": sorted(finding_ids, key=K.C),
             "verdict": verdict}
    if tamper == "predicate-value":
        pp = [dict(p) for p in proof["predicateProofs"]]
        pp[0]["value"] = {"true": "false", "false": "true",
                          "indeterminate": "true"}[pp[0]["value"]]
        proof["predicateProofs"] = pp
    proof_id = store.put_identity("proof-bundle", proof)

    evidence = {"schemaVersion": 2, "planId": plan_id,
                "viewIds": sorted(view_ids, key=K.C),
                "coverageIds": sorted(coverages, key=K.C),
                "importIds": list(plan["importIds"]),
                "findingIds": sorted(finding_ids, key=K.C),
                "proofBundleId": proof_id}
    evidence_id = store.put_identity("semantic-evidence", evidence)

    seal = {"schemaVersion": 2, "planId": plan_id, "executionPlanId": exec_plan_id,
            "evidenceId": evidence_id, "evaluatorClosure": evaluator_closure_id,
            "policyDigest": policy_digest, "proofBundleId": proof_id,
            "verdict": verdict}
    seal_id = store.put_identity("evaluation-seal", seal)

    run = {"schemaVersion": 2, "projectId": B.PROJECT_ID, "snapshotId": snapshot_id,
           "planId": plan_id, "evidenceId": evidence_id,
           "evaluationSealId": seal_id,
           "capabilityManifestId": capability_manifest_id}
    run_id = store.put_identity("run", run)
    return {"runId": run_id, "run": run, "seal": seal, "evidence": evidence,
            "proof": proof, "replay": result, "ruleProgramDigest": rp_digest,
            "findings": findings_out}


def verify_replay(store, closed, expected):
    """Semantic proof replay: recompute the complete bundle from the RETAINED
    inputs and compare it to the retained claim.  A mismatch REFUSES."""
    facts = {fid: closed["facts"][fid] for fid in closed["facts"]}
    scopes = closed["scopes"]
    coverages = {cid: {"scopeId": c["scopeId"], "payload": c["payload"]}
                 for cid, c in closed["coverages"].items()}
    ulang = {}
    for uhex, (dom, u) in closed["universes"].items():
        ulang[uhex] = kit.DOMAIN_SETS["native-semantic-universe"][dom]["language"]
    view = EvalView(facts=facts, scopes=scopes, coverages=coverages,
                    universe_language=ulang)
    recomputed = replay(closed["policy"], closed["ruleProgram"],
                        closed["proof"]["ruleProgramDigest"], view,
                        closed["waivers"])
    diffs = []
    retained = closed["proof"]
    if recomputed["verdict"] != retained["verdict"]:
        diffs.append(f"verdict: recomputed {recomputed['verdict']} != retained "
                     f"{retained['verdict']}")
    rk = {(p["ruleId"], p["subjectId"], p["predicateId"]): p
          for p in recomputed["predicateProofs"]}
    tk = {(p["ruleId"], p["subjectId"], p["predicateId"]): p
          for p in retained["predicateProofs"]}
    if set(rk) != set(tk):
        diffs.append(f"predicate address set differs: {sorted(set(rk) ^ set(tk))}")
    for key in sorted(set(rk) & set(tk)):
        a, b = rk[key], tk[key]
        for field in ("operation", "value", "witnessDigest", "scopeIds"):
            if a[field] != b[field]:
                diffs.append(f"{key} {field}: recomputed {a[field]} != retained {b[field]}")
    rf = sorted((f["ruleId"], f["subject"]) for f in recomputed["findings"])
    tf = sorted((closed["findings"][fid]["finding"]["subjectId"],)
                for fid in closed["findings"])
    if len(rf) != len(tf):
        diffs.append(f"finding count: recomputed {len(rf)} != retained {len(tf)}")
    return {"ok": not diffs, "diffs": diffs, "recomputed": recomputed}
